The mission is planned to study Ganymede, Callisto, and Europa, three of Jupiter's Galilean moons. They are thought to have significant bodies of liquid water beneath their icy surfaces which would make them potentially habitable environments.The spacecraft was launched on 14 April 2023 at 12:14:36 UTC and is expected to reach Jupiter in July 2031 after four gravity assists and eight years of travel. In December 2034, the spacecraft will enter orbit around Ganymede for its close-up science mission. Its period of operations will overlap with NASA's Europa Clipper mission, launching in 2024.

Background
The mission started as a reformulation of the Jupiter Ganymede Orbiter proposal, which was to be ESA's component of the cancelled Europa Jupiter System Mission – Laplace (EJSM-Laplace). It became a candidate for the first L-class mission (L1) of the ESA Cosmic Vision Programme, and its selection was announced on 2 May 2012.In April 2012, JUICE was recommended over the proposed Advanced Telescope for High Energy Astrophysics (ATHENA) X-ray telescope and a gravitational wave observatory (New Gravitational wave Observatory (NGO)).In July 2015, Airbus Defence and Space was selected as the prime contractor to design and build the probe, to be assembled in Toulouse, France.

Spacecraft
The main spacecraft design drivers are related to the large distance to the Sun, the use of solar power, and Jupiter's harsh radiation environment. The orbit insertions at Jupiter and Ganymede and the large number of flyby manoeuvres (more than 25 gravity assists, and two Europa flybys) require the spacecraft to carry about 3,000 kg (6,600 lb) of chemical propellant.JUICE has a fixed 2.5 meter diameter high-gain antenna and a steerable medium-gain antenna, both X- and K-band will be used. Downlink rates of 2 Gb/day are possible with ground-based Deep Space Antennas. On-board data storage capability is 1.25 Tb.The JUICE main engine is a hypergolic bi-propellant (mono-methyl hydrazine and mixed oxides of nitrogen) 425 N thruster. A 100 kg multilayer insulation provides thermal control. The spacecraft is 3-axis stabilized using momentum wheels. Radiation shielding is used to protect onboard electronics from the Jovian environment.The JUICE science payload has a mass of 280 kg and includes the JANUS camera system, the MAJIS visible and infrared imaging spectrometer, the UVS ultraviolet imaging spectrograph, RIME radar sounder, GALA laser altimeter, SWI submillimetre wave instrument, J-MAG magnetometer, PEP particle and plasma package, RPWI radio and plasma wave investigation, 3GM radio science package, the PRIDE radio science instrument, and the RADEM radiation monitor. A 10.6-meter deployable boom will hold J-MAG and RPWI, a 16-meter-long deployable antenna will be used for RIME. Four 3-meter booms carry parts of the RPWI instrument. The other instruments are mounted on the spacecraft body, or for 3GM, within the spacecraft bus.

Timeline
Launch
JUICE was launched into space on 14 April 2023 from the Guiana Space Centre on an Ariane 5 rocket. This was the final launch of an ESA science mission using the Ariane 5 vehicle, and was the second to last launch of the rocket overall.The launch was originally scheduled for 13 April 2023, but due to poor weather the launch was postponed. The next day a second launch attempt succeeded, with liftoff occurring at 12:14:36 UTC. After the spacecraft separated from the rocket, it established a successful radio signal connection with the ground at 13:04 UTC. JUICE's solar arrays were deployed about half an hour later, prompting ESA to deem the launch a success.

Trajectory
Following the launch, there will be multiple planned gravity assists to put JUICE on a trajectory to Jupiter: a flyby of the Earth–Moon system in August 2024, Venus in August 2025, second flyby of Earth in September 2026, and a third and final flyby of Earth in January 2029.JUICE will pass through the asteroid belt twice. A flyby of the asteroid 223 Rosa has been proposed, and could occur in October 2029.Gravity assists include:
Interplanetary transfer (Earth, Venus, Earth, Earth)
Jupiter orbit insertion and apocentre reduction with multiple Ganymede gravity assists
Reduction of velocity with Ganymede–Callisto assists
Increase inclination with 10–12 Callisto gravity assists

Arrival at the Jovian system
When it arrives in Jupiter's system in July 2031, JUICE will first perform a flyby of Ganymede in preparation for Jupiter orbital insertion about 7.5 hours later. The first orbit will be elongated, with subsequent orbits gradually lowered over time, resulting in a circular orbit around Jupiter.The first Europa flyby will take place in July 2032. JUICE will enter a high inclination orbit to allow exploration of Jupiter's polar regions and to study Jupiter's magnetosphere.

Orbital insertion on Ganymede
In December 2034, JUICE will enter an elliptical orbit around Ganymede. The first orbit will be at a distance of 5,000 km (3,100 mi). In 2035, JUICE will enter a circular orbit 500 km (310 mi) above the surface of Ganymede. JUICE will study Ganymede's composition and magnetosphere among other things.

Planned deorbit on Ganymede
When the spacecraft consumes its remaining propellant, JUICE is planned to be deorbited and impact Ganymede at the end of 2035.

Science objectives
The JUICE orbiter will perform detailed investigations on Ganymede and evaluate its potential to support life. Investigations of Europa and Callisto will complete a comparative picture of these Galilean moons. The three moons are thought to harbour internal liquid water oceans, and so are central to understanding the habitability of icy worlds.
The main science objectives for Ganymede, and to a lesser extent for Callisto, are:
Characterisation of the ocean layers and detection of putative subsurface water reservoirs
Topographical, geological and compositional mapping of the surface
Study of the physical properties of the icy crusts
Characterisation of the internal mass distribution, dynamics and evolution of the interiors
Investigation of Ganymede's tenuous atmosphere
Study of Ganymede's intrinsic magnetic field and its interactions with the Jovian magnetosphere.For Europa, the focus is on the chemistry essential to life, including organic molecules, and on understanding the formation of surface features and the composition of the non-water-ice material. Furthermore, JUICE will provide the first subsurface sounding of the moon, including the first determination of the minimal thickness of the icy crust over the most recently volcanically active regions.
More distant spatially resolved observations will also be carried out for several minor irregular satellites and the volcanically active moon Io.

Science instruments
On 21 February 2013, after a competition, 11 science instruments were selected by ESA, which were developed by science and engineering teams from all over Europe, with participation from the US. Japan also contributed several components for SWI, RPWI, GALA, PEP, JANUS and J-MAG instruments, and will facilitate testing.

A camera system to image Ganymede and interesting parts of the surface of Callisto at better than 400 m/pixel (resolution limited by mission data volume). JIMO was to have a large number of revolutionary features. Throughout its main voyage to the Jupiter moons, it was to be propelled by an ion propulsion system via either the  High Power Electric Propulsion or NEXIS engine, and powered by a small fission reactor.

{"final_story":"Baik, mari kita bayangkan ini adalah kelas sains di SMA. Aku akan menjadi pemandumu, dan kalian semua adalah siswa-siswi yang siap menjelajahi luar angkasa!

***

**Budi (Siswa):** Delapan tahun, Bu? Lama sekali! Apa yang membuat perjalanannya begitu lama?

**Ibu Indah:** Pertanyaan bagus, Budi! Perjalanan ke Jupiter itu jauh sekali, puluhan juta kilometer! JUICE tidak bisa langsung meluncur cepat ke sana. Ia harus menggunakan teknik yang disebut "bantuan gravitasi" dari Bumi dan Venus. Ibaratnya, ia menumpang kecepatan dari planet-planet ini untuk kemudian dihempaskan menuju Jupiter, menghemat bahan bakar.

**Ibu Indah:** Tepat sekali, Ayu! Meskipun JUICE akan mengelilingi Jupiter dan mempelajari atmosfer serta medan magnetnya yang dahsyat, fokus utamanya adalah investigasi terhadap **bulan-bulan es Jupiter**. Itulah mengapa nama misinya ada "Icy moons"-nya.

**Rifa (Siswa):** Bulan-bulan es? Apakah sama dengan bulan kita, Bu?

**Ibu Indah:** Nah, ini yang menarik, Rifa! Jupiter memiliki banyak bulan, tapi ada empat yang paling besar dan terkenal, disebut bulan Galilea, karena ditemukan oleh Galileo Galilei. Ketiga bulan yang akan menjadi target utama JUICE adalah **Ganymede, Callisto, dan Europa**.

(Ibu Indah menggeser slide, menampilkan gambar ketiga bulan tersebut.)

**Ibu Indah:** Perhatikan ketiga bulan ini. Apa yang kalian lihat?

**Dina (Siswa):** Mereka semua terlihat seperti bola es, Bu. Ada retakan-retakan di beberapa permukaannya.

**Ibu Indah:** Pengamatan yang sangat jeli, Dina! Permukaan ketiga bulan ini memang dilapisi es. Tapi, di sinilah letak misterinya, dan inilah **objektif utama sains dari misi JUICE**: para ilmuwan menduga kuat bahwa di bawah lapisan es yang tebal ini, terdapat **samudra air cair yang sangat besar!**

**Budi:** Samudra air cair? Di luar angkasa? Di bulan yang berjarak miliaran kilometer dari Matahari? Bagaimana bisa, Bu?

Diduga, panas internal dari bulan-bulan ini, mungkin akibat gaya tarik-ulur gravitasi Jupiter yang sangat kuat (disebut 'tidal heating'), menjaga air di bawah es tetap cair. Dan kalian tahu apa arti air cair dalam konteks astrobiologi?

**Ayu:** Kemungkinan adanya kehidupan, Bu!

**Ibu Indah:** Seratus persen, Ayu! Itulah mengapa misi ini sangat penting. Jika ada air cair, apalagi dalam jumlah samudra, potensi untuk menemukan lingkungan yang layak huni, atau bahkan tanda-tanda kehidupan di luar Bumi, menjadi sangat tinggi. 1.  **Memetakan permukaan:** Dengan kamera dan spektrometer, ia akan membuat peta topografi, geologi, dan komposisi bulan-bulan tersebut. Kita ingin tahu terbuat dari apa permukaannya, seperti apa kawah-kawahnya, dan bukti-bukti aktivitas geologis di masa lalu.

4.  **Menyelidiki atmosfer Ganymede:** Ganymede adalah satu-satunya bulan di Tata Surya yang punya medan magnet sendiri! Ini sangat unik. JUICE akan mempelajari atmosfer tipisnya dan bagaimana medan magnet Ganymede berinteraksi dengan medan magnet raksasa Jupiter.

**Ayu:** Bagaimana dengan Europa, Bu? Sepertinya Europa sering dibicarakan dalam kaitannya dengan kehidupan.

**Ibu Indah:** Europa memang sangat menarik, Ayu! Ada misi lain dari NASA, yaitu Europa Clipper, yang juga akan mempelajari bulan ini. Untuk **Europa**, fokus JUICE sedikit berbeda. Ia akan:
1.  **Mempelajari kimia yang penting bagi kehidupan:** Mencari molekul organik dan memahami komposisi material non-es di permukaannya. Jika ada sesuatu yang keluar dari retakan es, kita ingin tahu apa isinya.
2.  **Menentukan ketebalan minimum kerak es:** Ini penting untuk memahami seberapa mudah material dari samudra di bawahnya bisa mencapai permukaan, atau sebaliknya. JUICE akan melakukan "subsurface sounding" pertama kali di Europa.

**Budi:** Jadi, singkatnya, JUICE mencari air cair dan tanda-tanda kehidupan di bawah es?

**Ibu Indah:** Itu inti besarnya, Budi! Dengan kata lain, JUICE sedang mencari **lingkungan yang layak huni** di luar Bumi. Ganymede, Callisto, dan Europa adalah kandidat terkuat di Tata Surya kita untuk menyimpan samudra bawah permukaan, dan JUICE akan memberikan gambaran komparatif dari ketiga dunia es ini. Ini seperti membandingkan tiga laboratorium alami yang berbeda.

**Dina:** Kapan JUICE akan sampai ke Ganymede, Bu?

**Ibu Indah:** JUICE akan tiba di sistem Jupiter pada Juli 2031, dan setelah beberapa manuver dan terbang lintas, dia akan **memasuki orbit Ganymede pada Desember 2034**. Itu adalah momen bersejarah, karena JUICE akan menjadi kapal antariksa pertama yang mengorbit bulan Jupiter selain Jupiter itu sendiri!

**Ibu Indah:** Setelah mengamati dan mengumpulkan data selama sekitar satu tahun di orbit Ganymede, JUICE akan kehabisan bahan bakar dan dijadwalkan untuk sengaja dijatuhkan dan menabrak Ganymede itu sendiri di akhir 2035. Agar tidak ada risiko kontaminasi di masa depan.

**Ibu Indah:** Jadi, tim, apakah kalian sekarang mengerti betapa pentingnya misi JUICE ini? Ini adalah langkah besar dalam pencarian kita akan pemahaman yang lebih dalam tentang alam semesta, dan mungkin, tentang posisi kita di dalamnya. Mungkin suatu hari, salah satu dari kalian yang akan menjadi ilmuwan yang menganalisis data-data dari JUICE ini!

(Siswa-siswa mengangguk, beberapa terlihat bersemangat. Mereka mulai menulis catatan di buku.)

***

**Poin-Poin Penting untuk Siswa (Rekap):**

*   **Apa itu JUICE?** Kapal antariksa penjelajah dari ESA yang diluncurkan pada 14 April 2023. Akan tiba di Jupiter pada Juli 2031 setelah perjalanan 8 tahun.

    *   **Europa:** Bulan yang sangat menarik perhatian karena potensi kehidupannya.

“As you know,” Dr. Thorne continued, “Jupiter is a giant of our solar system, but it’s not just the planet itself that holds mysteries. Orbiting this gas giant are some of the most intriguing bodies in our cosmic neighbourhood – the Galilean moons.”

He waved a hand, and three spheres appeared, orbiting the holographic Jupiter. Each glowed with a faint, internal light.

“These three beauties,” Dr. Thorne pointed, “are Ganymede, Callisto, and Europa. And they are the stars of the JUICE mission. What makes them so special, you ask?” He paused for dramatic effect, then answered his own question. “We believe they harbour massive, hidden oceans of liquid water beneath their icy crusts!”

A ripple of murmurs went through the virtual classroom. The possibility of subsurface oceans was always a hot topic.

“Now, let’s dive into JUICE’s main scientific objectives,” Dr. Thorne said, bringing up a series of bullet points. “First and foremost, JUICE aims to perform *detailed investigations of Ganymede*. Why Ganymede, the largest moon in the solar system, you ask? Because Ganymede is truly unique – it’s the only moon we know of that generates its own magnetic field, a miniature version of Jupiter’s!”

He highlighted the objectives for Ganymede:

*   **Characterizing its ocean layers and searching for other subsurface water reservoirs.** “Imagine finding not just one, but multiple hidden oceans!” Dr. Thorne exclaimed.
*   **Mapping its surface – its topography, geology, and composition.** “Think of it like creating a detailed treasure map of an alien world,” he added.

*   **Investigating its tenuous atmosphere.** “Does it even have one? If so, what’s it made of?”
*   **Analyzing its intrinsic magnetic field and how it interacts with Jupiter’s colossal magnetosphere.** “This is crucial to understanding Ganymede’s uniqueness!”

“While Ganymede is our primary focus for much of the mission,” Dr. Thorne explained, “JUICE will also conduct crucial investigations of Europa and Callisto to get a comprehensive picture of these icy worlds.”

He brought up a separate set of objectives for Europa:

*   **Focusing on the chemistry essential to life, including organic molecules.** “Because if there’s an ocean, and there are organic molecules, the question of life gets a whole lot more interesting!”
*   **Understanding the formation of its surface features and the composition of its non-water-ice material.** “Europa’s surface is cracked and chaotic, revealing clues about its powerful internal forces.”
*   **Providing the first subsurface sounding of the moon, including determining the minimal thickness of its icy crust over volcanically active regions.** “This is huge! We want to know exactly how deep we’d have to drill to reach that ocean.”

“And Callisto?” a student named Maya asked from the back.

Dr. Thorne smiled. “Excellent question, Maya! While Callisto might seem less dynamic than its siblings, JUICE will also contribute to understanding its ocean layers, geological features, and internal structure, just like we’ll do for Ganymede. “Patience, young explorers!” Dr. Thorne chuckled. “Space travel demands it. Once it reaches Jupiter, it will spend quite some time flying past all three moons, gathering data. It will spend its final year in close proximity to this magnetic moon, ultimately deorbiting and impacting its surface at the end of 2035, leaving its legacy of discovery behind.”

“So, in summary,” Dr. Thorne concluded, his avatar gesturing toward the three glowing moons, “the main science objectives of the JUICE mission are to thoroughly investigate Ganymede, explore Europa for potential habitability, and study Callisto for comparative analysis. All three of these incredible moons hold the promise of hidden oceans, and JUICE is our intrepid messenger, tasked with unlocking their secrets.”

The mission is planned to study Ganymede, Callisto, and Europa, three of Jupiter's Galilean moons. They are thought to have significant bodies of liquid water beneath their icy surfaces which would make them potentially habitable environments.The spacecraft was launched on 14 April 2023 at 12:14:36 UTC and is expected to reach Jupiter in July 2031 after four gravity assists and eight years of travel. In December 2034, the spacecraft will enter orbit around Ganymede for its close-up science mission. Its period of operations will overlap with NASA's Europa Clipper mission, launching in 2024.

Background
The mission started as a reformulation of the Jupiter Ganymede Orbiter proposal, which was to be ESA's component of the cancelled Europa Jupiter System Mission – Laplace (EJSM-Laplace). It became a candidate for the first L-class mission (L1) of the ESA Cosmic Vision Programme, and its selection was announced on 2 May 2012.In April 2012, JUICE was recommended over the proposed Advanced Telescope for High Energy Astrophysics (ATHENA) X-ray telescope and a gravitational wave observatory (New Gravitational wave Observatory (NGO)).In July 2015, Airbus Defence and Space was selected as the prime contractor to design and build the probe, to be assembled in Toulouse, France.

Spacecraft
The main spacecraft design drivers are related to the large distance to the Sun, the use of solar power, and Jupiter's harsh radiation environment. The orbit insertions at Jupiter and Ganymede and the large number of flyby manoeuvres (more than 25 gravity assists, and two Europa flybys) require the spacecraft to carry about 3,000 kg (6,600 lb) of chemical propellant.JUICE has a fixed 2.5 meter diameter high-gain antenna and a steerable medium-gain antenna, both X- and K-band will be used. Downlink rates of 2 Gb/day are possible with ground-based Deep Space Antennas. On-board data storage capability is 1.25 Tb.The JUICE main engine is a hypergolic bi-propellant (mono-methyl hydrazine and mixed oxides of nitrogen) 425 N thruster. A 100 kg multilayer insulation provides thermal control. The spacecraft is 3-axis stabilized using momentum wheels. Radiation shielding is used to protect onboard electronics from the Jovian environment.The JUICE science payload has a mass of 280 kg and includes the JANUS camera system, the MAJIS visible and infrared imaging spectrometer, the UVS ultraviolet imaging spectrograph, RIME radar sounder, GALA laser altimeter, SWI submillimetre wave instrument, J-MAG magnetometer, PEP particle and plasma package, RPWI radio and plasma wave investigation, 3GM radio science package, the PRIDE radio science instrument, and the RADEM radiation monitor. A 10.6-meter deployable boom will hold J-MAG and RPWI, a 16-meter-long deployable antenna will be used for RIME. Four 3-meter booms carry parts of the RPWI instrument. The other instruments are mounted on the spacecraft body, or for 3GM, within the spacecraft bus.

Timeline
Launch
JUICE was launched into space on 14 April 2023 from the Guiana Space Centre on an Ariane 5 rocket. This was the final launch of an ESA science mission using the Ariane 5 vehicle, and was the second to last launch of the rocket overall.The launch was originally scheduled for 13 April 2023, but due to poor weather the launch was postponed. The next day a second launch attempt succeeded, with liftoff occurring at 12:14:36 UTC. After the spacecraft separated from the rocket, it established a successful radio signal connection with the ground at 13:04 UTC. JUICE's solar arrays were deployed about half an hour later, prompting ESA to deem the launch a success.

Trajectory
Following the launch, there will be multiple planned gravity assists to put JUICE on a trajectory to Jupiter: a flyby of the Earth–Moon system in August 2024, Venus in August 2025, second flyby of Earth in September 2026, and a third and final flyby of Earth in January 2029.JUICE will pass through the asteroid belt twice. A flyby of the asteroid 223 Rosa has been proposed, and could occur in October 2029.Gravity assists include:
Interplanetary transfer (Earth, Venus, Earth, Earth)
Jupiter orbit insertion and apocentre reduction with multiple Ganymede gravity assists
Reduction of velocity with Ganymede–Callisto assists
Increase inclination with 10–12 Callisto gravity assists

Arrival at the Jovian system
When it arrives in Jupiter's system in July 2031, JUICE will first perform a flyby of Ganymede in preparation for Jupiter orbital insertion about 7.5 hours later. The first orbit will be elongated, with subsequent orbits gradually lowered over time, resulting in a circular orbit around Jupiter.The first Europa flyby will take place in July 2032. JUICE will enter a high inclination orbit to allow exploration of Jupiter's polar regions and to study Jupiter's magnetosphere.

Orbital insertion on Ganymede
In December 2034, JUICE will enter an elliptical orbit around Ganymede. The first orbit will be at a distance of 5,000 km (3,100 mi). In 2035, JUICE will enter a circular orbit 500 km (310 mi) above the surface of Ganymede. JUICE will study Ganymede's composition and magnetosphere among other things.

Planned deorbit on Ganymede
When the spacecraft consumes its remaining propellant, JUICE is planned to be deorbited and impact Ganymede at the end of 2035.

Science objectives
The JUICE orbiter will perform detailed investigations on Ganymede and evaluate its potential to support life. Investigations of Europa and Callisto will complete a comparative picture of these Galilean moons. The three moons are thought to harbour internal liquid water oceans, and so are central to understanding the habitability of icy worlds.
The main science objectives for Ganymede, and to a lesser extent for Callisto, are:
Characterisation of the ocean layers and detection of putative subsurface water reservoirs
Topographical, geological and compositional mapping of the surface
Study of the physical properties of the icy crusts
Characterisation of the internal mass distribution, dynamics and evolution of the interiors
Investigation of Ganymede's tenuous atmosphere
Study of Ganymede's intrinsic magnetic field and its interactions with the Jovian magnetosphere.For Europa, the focus is on the chemistry essential to life, including organic molecules, and on understanding the formation of surface features and the composition of the non-water-ice material. Furthermore, JUICE will provide the first subsurface sounding of the moon, including the first determination of the minimal thickness of the icy crust over the most recently volcanically active regions.
More distant spatially resolved observations will also be carried out for several minor irregular satellites and the volcanically active moon Io.

On 21 February 2013, after a competition, 11 science instruments were selected by ESA, which were developed by science and engineering teams from all over Europe, with participation from the US. Background
The mission started as a reformulation of the Jupiter Ganymede Orbiter proposal, which was to be ESA's component of the cancelled Europa Jupiter System Mission – Laplace (EJSM-Laplace). It became a candidate for the first L-class mission (L1) of the ESA Cosmic Vision Programme, and its selection was announced on 2 May 2012.In April 2012, JUICE was recommended over the proposed Advanced Telescope for High Energy Astrophysics (ATHENA) X-ray telescope and a gravitational wave observatory (New Gravitational wave Observatory (NGO)).In July 2015, Airbus Defence and Space was selected as the prime contractor to design and build the probe, to be assembled in Toulouse, France.

The main spacecraft design drivers are related to the large distance to the Sun, the use of solar power, and Jupiter's harsh radiation environment. The orbit insertions at Jupiter and Ganymede and the large number of flyby manoeuvres (more than 25 gravity assists, and two Europa flybys) require the spacecraft to carry about 3,000 kg (6,600 lb) of chemical propellant.JUICE has a fixed 2.5 meter diameter high-gain antenna and a steerable medium-gain antenna, both X- and K-band will be used. Interplanetary transfer (Earth, Venus, Earth, Earth)
Jupiter orbit insertion and apocentre reduction with multiple Ganymede gravity assists
Reduction of velocity with Ganymede–Callisto assists
Increase inclination with 10–12 Callisto gravity assists

When it arrives in Jupiter's system in July 2031, JUICE will first perform a flyby of Ganymede in preparation for Jupiter orbital insertion about 7.5 hours later. The first orbit will be elongated, with subsequent orbits gradually lowered over time, resulting in a circular orbit around Jupiter.The first Europa flyby will take place in July 2032. JUICE will enter a high inclination orbit to allow exploration of Jupiter's polar regions and to study Jupiter's magnetosphere.

In December 2034, JUICE will enter an elliptical orbit around Ganymede. The first orbit will be at a distance of 5,000 km (3,100 mi). When the spacecraft consumes its remaining propellant, JUICE is planned to be deorbited and impact Ganymede at the end of 2035.

Topographical, geological and compositional mapping of the surface
Study of the physical properties of the icy crusts
Characterisation of the internal mass distribution, dynamics and evolution of the interiors
Investigation of Ganymede's tenuous atmosphere

**Proyek “Bayangan Langit”**

Desas-desus berawal di kelas Ilmu Pengetahuan Alam Pak Ardi. Hari itu, topik diskusi adalah tentang alat-alat pengumpul data cuaca.

"Siapa yang bisa memberi tahu saya, alat apa yang biasa digunakan untuk memprediksi cuaca?" tanya Pak Ardi, sambil tersenyum ke arah seisi kelas.

Bella, siswa yang selalu bersemangat, mengangkat tangannya. "Balon cuaca, Pak! Biasanya kecil dan dilepaskan ke atmosfer untuk mengukur suhu, tekanan, dan kelembaban."

"Tepat sekali, Bella!" Pak Ardi mengangguk. "Tapi, bagaimana jika ada sebuah balon yang ukurannya jauh lebih besar dari balon cuaca biasa, dan justru terbang di atas beberapa negara tanpa izin?"

Sontak, seluruh kelas hening. Pak Ardi kemudian memutar sebuah video pendek. Video itu menunjukkan sebuah benda putih besar melayang di langit biru.

"Ini adalah 'Balon Misteri' yang menjadi berita utama awal tahun ini," Pak Ardi memulai ceritanya. "Balon ini milik Tiongkok, dan terlihat di wilayah udara Amerika Utara dari akhir Januari hingga awal Februari 2023."

Rizal, siswa yang selalu penasaran dengan teknologi, bertanya, "Tapi, Pak, kenapa balon Tiongkok bisa terbang di sana? Bukankah itu berarti melanggar kedaulatan negara lain?"

"Pertanyaan bagus, Rizal," jawab Pak Ardi. "Pemerintah Tiongkok mengklaim itu adalah balon sipil, kebanyakan untuk tujuan meteorologi, yang kebetulan terbawa angin. Namun, Amerika Serikat memiliki pandangan yang berbeda."

Pak Ardi berjalan ke papan tulis dan mulai menggambar. "Bayangkan ini adalah balon raksasa itu." Dia menggambar sebuah lingkaran besar. "Para pejabat AS mengatakan bahwa ukuran balon ini sangatlah masif. Tingginya sekitar 61 meter. Itu kira-kira setinggi gedung 20 lantai!"

Mata para siswa terbelalak. "Wow!" seru beberapa dari mereka.

"Diameter balonnya sendiri sekitar 45 meter," lanjut Pak Ardi. "Bahkan para ahli mengatakan balon cuaca biasa ukurannya kurang dari seperempat dari diameter balon ini. Jadi, ini jelas bukan balon cuaca biasa."

Sekar, yang terkenal kritis, bertanya, "Kalau bukan balon cuaca biasa, lalu apa isinya, Pak?"

Pak Ardi tersenyum teka-teki. "Nah, itu dia bagian yang paling menarik. Bagian penting dari balon ini adalah 'muatannya' atau yang sering disebut sebagai 'payload'. Payload ini adalah semacam wadah teknologi yang digantung di bawah balon." Dia menggambar sebuah kotak besar di bawah lingkaran balon.

"Bayangkan ukuran payload ini," kata Pak Ardi. "Menurut perkiraan awal, ukurannya sebesar dua hingga tiga bus sekolah!"

"Dua bus sekolah?!" seru Bima, terkejut. "Besar sekali!"

"Benar sekali, Bima. Dan bobotnya? Diperkirakan lebih dari 910 kilogram!" Pak Ardi menambahkan. "Bahkan Presiden AS Joe Biden menggambarkannya sebagai membawa peralatan mata-mata seberat dua gerbong kereta api!"

Siswa-siswa saling berbisik, kagum dengan informasi tersebut.

"Apa yang ada di dalam payload sebesar itu, Pak?" tanya Bella lagi.

"Setelah balon itu ditembak jatuh dan serpihannya dikumpulkan, para ahli menganalisisnya di laboratorium FBI. Mereka menemukan bahwa payload itu dilengkapi dengan antena dan peralatan lain yang kemungkinan digunakan untuk mengumpulkan sinyal komunikasi. Sinyal intelijen, lho," jelas Pak Ardi. "Ada juga panel surya yang terpasang pada payload, jumlahnya sampai enam belas buah, untuk memberikan daya pada seluruh peralatan canggih itu."

Rian, yang selalu memperhatikan detail teknis, bertanya, "Kalau begitu, bagaimana balon sebesar itu bergerak, Pak? Apa terbawa angin saja?"

"Lagi-lagi pertanyaan yang bagus, Rian!" Pak Ardi menunjuk ke gambar di papan tulis. "Meskipun Tiongkok mengklaimnya terbawa angin, pejabat AS mengatakan balon itu memiliki baling-baling dan kemudi. Jadi, balon ini sebenarnya bisa bermanuver, meskipun kemampuan kendalinya terbatas."

Pak Ardi kemudian menjelaskan lebih jauh. "Balon ini jenis 'superpressure balloon'. Artinya, volumenya relatif konstan walaupun ada perubahan tekanan atau suhu di luar. Ini yang membuat balon tersebut bisa mempertahankan ketinggian dengan lebih baik dan terbang jauh lebih lama dibandingkan balon biasa."

"Tapi Pak, kalau memang sebesar itu dan bisa mengumpulkan informasi, kenapa pemerintah AS membiarkannya terbang dulu?" tanya Sekar.

"Itu juga pertanyaan yang sempat muncul ke publik," jawab Pak Ardi. "Pentagon mengatakan balon itu tidak menimbulkan ancaman militer atau fisik bagi orang-orang di darat. Menembak jatuh di atas air dianggap lebih aman dan memberikan peluang lebih besar untuk mempelajari puing-puingnya nanti untuk tujuan intelijen."

Akhirnya, pada tanggal 4 Februari 2023, Angkatan Udara AS menembak jatuh balon tersebut di atas perairan teritorial AS di lepas pantai Carolina Selatan. Puing-puingnya kemudian dikumpulkan untuk analisis lebih lanjut.

"Insiden ini memperlihatkan betapa canggihnya teknologi pengawasan udara yang ada saat ini," tutup Pak Ardi. "Meskipun satelit dan drone sudah umum, balon masih memiliki beberapa keunggulan, seperti biaya yang lebih rendah dan kemampuan untuk berlama-lama di suatu area. Dan yang terpenting, insiden ini meningkatkan ketegangan antara Amerika Serikat dan Tiongkok, menunjukkan pentingnya kedaulatan wilayah udara sebuah negara."

Background
History and development of reconnaissance balloons
Balloons have been valued for their ability to observe the battlefield and direct artillery. Their usage peaked during World War I, after which they were increasingly replaced by airplanes. The 2023 balloon incident occurred while U.S.–China relations were at their worst in decades, following suspected incidents of Chinese espionage and amid increasing strategic competition in military and economic sectors. In 2022, the United States, along with some of its allies, imposed stringent export controls on "foundational technologies", such as semiconductor microprocessors, to China in order to hamper the latter's development of advanced technology and military tools. Sekar, yang terkenal kritis, bertanya, "Kalau bukan balon cuaca biasa, lalu apa isinya, Pak?"

Pak Ardi tersenyum teka-teki. "Nah, itu dia bagian yang paling menarik. Bagian penting dari balon ini adalah 'muatannya' atau yang sering disebut sebagai 'payload'. Payload ini adalah semacam wadah teknologi yang digantung di bawah balon." Dia menggambar sebuah kotak besar di bawah lingkaran balon.

"Bayangkan ukuran payload ini," kata Pak Ardi. "Menurut perkiraan awal, ukurannya sebesar dua hingga tiga bus sekolah!"

"Apa yang ada di dalam payload sebesar itu, Pak?" tanya Bella lagi.

"Setelah balon itu ditembak jatuh dan serpihannya dikumpulkan, para ahli menganalisisnya di laboratorium FBI. "Insiden ini memperlihatkan betapa canggihnya teknologi pengawasan udara yang ada saat ini," tutup Pak Ardi. "Meskipun satelit dan drone sudah umum, balon masih memiliki beberapa keunggulan, seperti biaya yang lebih rendah dan kemampuan untuk berlama-lama di suatu area. Background
History and development of reconnaissance balloons
Balloons have been valued for their ability to observe the battlefield and direct artillery. Their usage peaked during World War I, after which they were increasingly replaced by airplanes. By 2019, the Pentagon had invested millions in COLD STAR (Covert Long Dwell Stratospheric Architecture), a project for stealthy balloons that are now being transitioned from narcotics surveillance into military service. China recognizes the importance of catching up to foreign countries in this domain. Its military publications have highlighted the use of balloons to assess the early warning and response capabilities of enemy air defenses and to enhance China's own defense capabilities.

In 2020 and 2021, similar balloons were sighted in Sendai and Hachinohe, Japan respectively, but they were not identified as of Chinese origin at the time. A similar aircraft was sighted in January 2022 over India's strategically important Andaman and Nicobar islands. In February 2022, several balloons were detected off the coast of Taiwan, which their Ministry of National Defense said were likely for meteorological observations for the PLA's Eastern Theater Command. Another crashed near Taiwan in February 2023, carrying an antenna, a transmitter, temperature and humidity sensors, and was likely from China as well.

U.S.–China tensions
The 2023 balloon incident occurred while U.S.–China relations were at their worst in decades, following suspected incidents of Chinese espionage and amid increasing strategic competition in military and economic sectors. In 2022, the United States, along with some of its allies, imposed stringent export controls on "foundational technologies", such as semiconductor microprocessors, to China in order to hamper the latter's development of advanced technology and military tools. The US has also sought to maintain critical supply chains independent from China.

Balloon
Size, propulsion, and payload
The balloon carried an underslung payload described as a "technology bay" estimated to be the size of "two or three school buses" and was powered by sixteen solar arrays mounted on the payload. AI startup Synthetaic, using image data from Planet Labs spacecraft, reported the balloon's diameter as 148 feet (45 m). USNORTHCOM and NORAD Commander, General Glen VanHerck, estimated the payload weighed more than 2,000 pounds (910 kg).The Chinese balloon was a superpressure balloon similar to earlier NASA designs, where the volume of the balloon is kept relatively constant in the face of changes in ambient pressure outside the balloon, and the temperature of the contained lifting gas. This allows better altitude control and much longer endurance compared to the more common variable-volume balloon design.
National Security Council spokesman Admiral John Kirby said the craft had a propeller and could be maneuvered. U.S. officials told foreign diplomats in Beijing that the craft had rudders and propellers. A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson said it had "limited self-steering capability".The U.S. Department of Defense said the balloon did not present a military or physical threat to people on the ground while it remained in the air, and that shooting it down over water would be safer and increased the opportunity to study the wreckage for intelligence purposes.Citing a PLA procurement portal, a U.S. official said that the balloon was manufactured by a civilian Chinese defense contractor.

Signals intelligence capabilities
Experts noted that weather balloons typically are about 20 feet (6 m) wide, less than a quarter of the balloon's diameter. Those interviewed by BBC News said it was unusual for weather balloons to last as long as the one involved in the incident and that the balloon "might have been more sophisticated than China claims".Images from U-2 flybys and forensic analysis of the payload showed antennas that likely were used for collecting and transmitting signals intelligence. The report also notes that a team of Saudi operatives, who were part of the crown prince's security detail, carried out the operation. On February 4, the U.S. Air Force shot down the balloon over U.S. territorial waters off the coast of South Carolina. Debris from the wreckage was recovered and sent to the FBI Laboratory in Quantico, Virginia, for analysis. Following a preliminary analysis of the debris in June, U.S. officials stated that the balloon carried intelligence gathering equipment but does not appear to have sent information back to China. U.S. president Biden described the balloon as carrying two railroad cars' equivalent of spy equipment; his government said the balloon had a propeller for maneuverability.When the object was first spotted, the Pentagon characterized it as a surveillance balloon. The Chinese government maintained it was a civilian (mainly meteorological) airship that had been blown off course. According to U.S. officials, the balloon carried antennas and other equipment capable of geolocating communications signals, and similar balloons from China have flown over more than 40 nations. Analysts said that its flight path and structural characteristics were dissimilar from those of a typical weather balloon. American officials later disclosed that they had been tracking the balloon since it was launched from Hainan and its original destinations were likely Guam and Hawaii, but prevailing winds blew it off course and across North America.The incident increased U.S.–China tensions. The United States called the balloon's presence a violation of its sovereignty, and its Secretary of State Antony Blinken postponed a long-awaited diplomatic visit to Beijing. Canada summoned the Chinese ambassador in response to the incident.In the United States, three other high-altitude objects, over Northern Alaska (February 10), Yukon (February 11), and Lake Huron (February 11–12) respectively, were detected and subsequently shot down; a later assessment said they had no relation to China.

Background
History and development of reconnaissance balloons
Balloons have been valued for their ability to observe the battlefield and direct artillery. Their usage peaked during World War I, after which they were increasingly replaced by airplanes. During the Cold War, the United States sent hundreds of high-altitude balloons, ostensibly for "meteorological survey" under Project Genetrix, over China and other Eastern Bloc countries to gain intelligence on their nuclear capabilities, drawing their protests.Although mostly supplanted by surveillance satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles, balloons have retained some advantages, such as a lower cost of production and deployment. By 2019, the Pentagon had invested millions in COLD STAR (Covert Long Dwell Stratospheric Architecture), a project for stealthy balloons that are now being transitioned from narcotics surveillance into military service. China recognizes the importance of catching up to foreign countries in this domain. Its military publications have highlighted the use of balloons to assess the early warning and response capabilities of enemy air defenses and to enhance China's own defense capabilities.

Past Chinese balloons and unidentified objects
Suspected Chinese surveillance balloons had been detected in U.S. airspace in the past, namely over Guam, Hawaii, and Florida. One occurred earlier during Joe Biden's presidency (2021–present) and three occurred during Donald Trump's presidency (2017–2021). They did not persist as long as the 2023 incident, and China was able to recover those balloons.Other pre-2023 incursions have remained unexplained, classified by U.S. authorities as unidentified aerial phenomena. **Gelombang Badai di Tanah Emas: Kisah Perang Saudara Myanmar**

Sore itu, di sudut kafe sekolah, Maya dan Rian sedang serius membaca berita di tablet Bima. Topik utamanya adalah konflik di Myanmar. Kening Maya berkerut. "Bima, aku sering dengar tentang Myanmar, tapi konflik ini... sungguh kompleks. Bisa jelaskan apa yang sebenarnya terjadi di sana?"

**Awal Mula Badai: Kudeta 2021**

"Inti dari konflik yang sedang berlangsung ini adalah peristiwa yang terjadi pada **1 Februari 2021**," Bima memulai. "Tentu saja, rakyat Myanmar tidak tinggal diam," lanjut Bima. "Ribuan orang turun ke jalan, melakukan protes damai menentang kudeta. Tapi, militer merespons dengan kekerasan luar biasa. Penindasan berdarah ini justru memicu sesuatu yang tak terduga."

"Protes damai berubah menjadi perlawanan bersenjata," jelas Bima. "Banyak warga sipil yang semula hanya berdemo, mulai mencari cara untuk membela diri. "Wow, itu banyak!" seru Rian.

"Dan pengamat independen percaya angka sebenarnya jauh lebih tinggi," tambah Bima. "Diperkirakan hanya sekitar 72 dari 330 township dan beberapa kota besar saja yang masih dikendalikan penuh oleh junta militer. **Dampak Paling Mengenaskan: Pengungsian Internal**

"Lalu, bagaimana nasib rakyat sipil di tengah semua ini?" tanya Maya dengan nada prihatin.

Bima menghela napas. "Inilah bagian yang paling memilukan. Pertempuran sengit, kekerasan militer, dan penyerangan ke desa-desa telah menyebabkan krisis kemanusiaan yang sangat besar. Banyak sekali orang yang terpaksa meninggalkan rumah mereka untuk mencari keselamatan."

"Berapa banyak orang yang diperkirakan mengungsi?" Rian bertanya, melihat ke Bima dengan serius.

"Menurut PBB, pada **Maret 2023**, semenjak kudeta, sekitar **1,6 juta orang telah menjadi pengungsi internal (internally displaced persons/IDPs)** di dalam Myanmar," jelas Bima datar. "Bayangkan, 1,6 juta orang kehilangan rumah, mata pencarian, dan hidup dalam ketidakpastian. Angka ini naik dari 1,3 juta pada September 2022. Selain itu, lebih dari 13.000 anak-anak telah tewas, dan 55.000 bangunan sipil hancur. Bahkan, lebih dari 40.000 orang juga telah melarikan diri ke negara-negara tetangga."

Maya dan Rian terdiam, membayangkan jumlah yang begitu besar.

"Jadi," Rian merangkum, "saat ini Myanmar sedang dilanda perang saudara berskala besar antara junta militer dan pemerintahan sipil NUG bersama PDF serta beberapa EAOs. Junta militer kehilangan kendali signifikan atas sebagian besar wilayah, dan dampaknya, jutaan orang terpaksa mengungsi."

"Tepat sekali," Bima mengangguk. "Ini adalah konflik yang kompleks, dengan akar sejarah panjang pemberontakan etnis, yang semakin diperparah oleh kudeta dan respons brutal militer. Rakyat Myanmar, terutama warga sipil, adalah korban sejati dari Gelombang Badai di Tanah Emas ini. Penting bagi kita untuk terus mengikuti perkembangannya dan memahami perjuangan mereka."

"Berapa banyak orang yang diperkirakan mengungsi?" Rian bertanya, melihat ke Bima dengan serius.

{"metric":"answer_relevancy","model":"google/gemini-2.5-flash","system_prompt":"","user_input":"Pembuatan cerita dari teks berikut: Buat cerita edukatif yang membantu siswa memahami: What is the current status of the Myanmar civil war, and how many people have been internally displaced since the coup?","contexts_count":2,"contexts":["The Myanmar civil war (Burmese: ၂၀၂၁-၂၀၂၃ မြန်မာနိုင်ငံ ပြည်သူ့ခုခံတွန်းလှန်စစ်), also called the Myanmar Spring Revolution, and the People's Defensive War, is an ongoing civil war following Myanmar's long-running insurgencies which escalated significantly in response to the 2021 military coup d'état and the subsequent violent crackdown on anti-coup protests.In the months following the coup, the opposition began to coalesce around the National Unity Government, which launched an offensive against the junta. By 2022, the opposition controlled substantial, though sparsely populated, territory. In many villages and towns, the junta's attacks drove out tens of thousands of people. On the second anniversary of the coup, in February 2023, the chairman of the State Administration Council, Min Aung Hlaing, admitted to losing stable control over "more than a third" of townships. Independent observers note the real number is likely far higher, with as few as 72 out of 330 townships and all major population centres remaining under stable control.As of September 2022, 1.3 million people have been internally displaced, and over 13,000 children have been killed. By March 2023, the UN estimated that since the coup, 17.6 million people in Myanmar required humanitarian assistance, while 1.6 million were internally displaced, and 55,000 civilian buildings had been destroyed. UNOCHA said that over 40,000 people fled into neighboring countries.

Background
On the morning of 1 February 2021, the Myanmar military, or Tatmadaw, successfully deposed the elected Myanmar government in a coup, forming a military junta. Former president Win Myint, Aung San Suu Kyi, and several other members of the National League for Democracy were detained during early morning raids and Min Aung Hlaing was placed as the Commander-in-Chief of Defence Services and de facto ruler of the nation.The exact motives behind the coup are unclear. In the leadup to the coup, the Tatmadaw claimed that the 2020 general elections had 8.6 million voter irregularities, but presented no evidence. The coup may have been a way to re-establish the military's long-reigning power over the country which ended ten years prior.The bloody repression of anti-coup demonstrations led to the creation of armed groups to fight the State Administration Council, the military junta. Gathered under the name of the People's Defence Force (PDF) and the orders of the National Unity Government (NUG), formed by former parliamentarians in office before the coup d'état, the PDF and the NUG officially declared a "defensive war" against the military regime in September 2021. The ACLED estimated that as of 29 July 2022, around 23,521 people in total had been killed in the violence following the 2021 coup.

Existing conflict
Insurgencies have been ongoing in Myanmar since 1948 and have largely been ethnic-based. Communist insurgencies and the Karen National Union were the primary opposition actors to the central government. Over the 20th century, several prominent ethnic armed organisations (EAOs) rose and fell in influence and control. Larger rebel factions such as the Kachin Independence Army formed in response to Ne Win's 1962 Burmese coup d'état and its increased political repression. The 8888 Uprising in response to the totalitarian rule of Ne Win resulted in some of the first modern Bamar militias forming from protestors heading to areas under ethnic rebel control.
In the aftermath of the 8888 Uprising, the State Law and Order Restoration Council, later called the State Peace and Development Council, formed a military junta. The Tatmadaw severely weakened ethnic insurgent groups, destroying most of their bases and strongholds through the 1990s. By the time of the 2011–2015 Myanmar political reforms, the junta had regained control of many long-time rebel strongholds including Kokang and Karen State.As part of its political reforms and democratization, the 2008 Constitution created self-administered zones with increased autonomy. In 2015, the Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement (NCA) was signed between 8 EAOs and the central government. However, as soon as 2018, the NCA had already begun to fall apart due to alleged violations of the agreement by Tatmadaw soldiers entering EAO territories to build roads. Many non-signatories continued the conflict. In late 2016, four non-signatories of the NCA formed the Northern Alliance, including the Kachin Independence Army and Arakan Army, engaged in war with the central government and other EAOs.

Prelude
Armed protestors
In late March, dozens of protesters had travelled to Myanmar's border areas to enlist in and train under one of the country's many insurgent groups, elevating the risk of a countrywide civil war. The Committee Representing Pyidaungsu Hluttaw also proposed the formation of a "federal armed force" to combat the military, and in late March the Arakan Army (AA) threatened to end its ceasefire with the military should the latter "persist in massacring civilians".During late March, protesters increasingly began arming themselves with homemade weapons such as guns in an attempt to defend themselves against attacks by the military. Simultaneously, clashes with soldiers and IED attacks against administrative buildings and police stations became more common as the trend of protesters using armed resistance rose.

Renewed ethnic conflict
The unrest across the nation and the increased need for junta troops in previously peaceful urban areas strengthened EAOs. The Kachin Independence Army (KIA) has already been on the offensive against the military since February and seized the military base of Alaw Bum near the town of Laiza on 25 March. The next day, the Karen National Liberation Army (KNLA) attacked a military base, killing 10 soldiers and taking others hostages in the first attack on the military since the protests began. The following day saw the 2021 Kalay clashes, the first openly armed resistance by protesters in the town of Kalay against the junta. Protestors used homemade weapons against soldiers and security forces attacking a protest camp.The military junta declared that it would cease all military operations on 29 March and hold bilateral negotiations with ethnic armed groups. However, the KIA continued its offensives stating that the Myanmar Army had continued operations as usual. Through April, the informal clashes intensified, such as on 8 April when protesters fought back against soldiers with hunting rifles and firebombs in a battle that resulted in 11 protesters' deaths. The same day, the country surpassed 600 deaths related to anti-coup protests since 1 February.Seven insurgent groups who were signatories to the Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement aligned themselves with the Committee Representing Pyidaungsu Hluttaw, including the All Burma Student Democratic Front and the Karen National Union. The Northern Alliance, comprising the Arakan Army, the Ta'ang National Liberation Army and the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army, attacked a police station in Naungmon, Shan State, killing at least 10 police officers and indicating their disregard of the junta's call for a ceasefire. In response, on 11 April, the junta military launched a counter-attack to recapture the Alaw Bum base using airstrikes and ground troops, but had to retreat amidst heavy casualties.

New conflicts
On 26 April, the Battle of Mindat became one of the first large-scale conflicts arising from the 2021 coup. The Chinland Defense Force (CDF) began armed resistance in Mindat, Chin State. As a response, the junta cut off food and water supplies and declared martial law. Fighting began when a group of demonstrators outside the town's Aung San statue requested the release of six of their arrested colleagues, when a soldier of the regime allegedly fired at someone, prompting protesters to react.

The military, armed with heavy weaponry and supported by armored vehicles, launched a brutal crackdown on the demonstrators. Tear gas, rubber bullets, and live ammunition were used indiscriminately, resulting in numerous casualties among the protesters. The streets of the town turned into a chaotic battleground, with fires burning and the sound of gunfire echoing through the air.

Despite the overwhelming force of the military, the protesters fought back with whatever they could find. They threw rocks, Molotov cocktails, and set up makeshift barricades to slow down the advancing troops. The clashes continued for hours, with both sides sustaining heavy losses.

As news of the violent clashes spread, more people from neighboring towns and villages joined the protest, swelling the ranks of the demonstrators. The military's attempts to quell the uprising only fueled the people's anger and determination to fight for their rights and freedom.

International condemnation poured in as reports of the brutal crackdown reached the global community. Calls for an immediate end to the violence and the release of all political prisoners grew louder. **Awal Mula Badai: Kudeta 2021**

"Inti dari konflik yang sedang berlangsung ini adalah peristiwa yang terjadi pada **1 Februari 2021**," Bima memulai. Anda sedang mengevaluasi Draf Cerita yang ditujukan untuk parameter berikut:
Target Usia Penonton: 15-18

Berikan ulasan kritis menggunakan format di bawah ini. Sajikan alasan Anda dalam bentuk paragraf yang mengalir dengan baik. Hindari penggunaan simbol khusus yang berlebihan. Pastikan setiap penilaian mencerminkan landasan teori yang disebutkan.

Panduan Jangkar Skor (Score Anchors) untuk Skala 1 hingga 5:
Untuk menjaga reliabilitas dan konsistensi penilaian otomatis (merujuk pada validitas rubrik analitik dalam sistem AWE menurut Fleckenstein et al., 2023), gunakan acuan rubrik berikut saat memberikan skor:
Skor 1 (Sangat Kurang): Bukti pemahaman atau kepatuhan sangat minim dan melenceng jauh dari tujuan atau instruksi dasar.
Skor 2 (Kurang): Ada upaya awal, tetapi memiliki kelemahan fundamental yang mengganggu pemahaman atau keluar dari kaidah target usia.
Skor 3 (Cukup): Memenuhi ekspektasi dasar, namun narasi atau nilai pendidikannya masih terasa kaku dan memerlukan revisi substansial.
Skor 4 (Baik): Konsep tersampaikan dengan baik, memenuhi standar pedagogis dan instruksi, dengan sedikit ruang untuk perbaikan minor.
Skor 5 (Sangat Baik): Eksekusi luar biasa, sangat menarik secara emosional, inovatif, dan sempurna dalam memenuhi instruksi serta teori pembelajaran.

Relevansi Tema dan Tujuan (Skor 1 hingga 5)
Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi mengenai seberapa kuat cerita ini berpijak pada permintaan awal dan tema yang dipilih. Analisis apakah konsep utama tersampaikan dengan jelas. (Landasan Teori: Prinsip "Constructive Alignment" dalam penilaian formatif, di mana tugas harus selaras dengan tujuan akhir pembelajaran, merujuk pada Morris et al., 2021).

Kesesuaian Usia, Kognitif, dan Scaffolding (Skor 1 hingga 5)
Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi mengenai tingkat kesulitan kosakata, struktur kalimat, dan kompleksitas alur. Nilai apakah elemen tersebut memberikan beban kognitif yang sesuai untuk target usia. Analisis juga apakah cerita memberikan "scaffolding" (perancah), yaitu membangun pemahaman dari konsep sederhana ke kompleks secara bertahap. (Landasan Teori: Manajemen beban kognitif dan desain pedagogis K-12 bertahap, merujuk pada Yue et al., 2022).

Keterlibatan Naratif dan Emosional (Skor 1 hingga 5)
Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi tentang kemampuan cerita dalam mempertahankan perhatian pembaca dan memicu rasa ingin tahu. Analisis kualitas deskripsi dan dinamika karakter. (Landasan Teori: Pentingnya stimulasi "Emotional and Behavioral Engagement" untuk mengoptimalkan penyerapan materi yang sering dievaluasi melalui kuesioner skala 5 poin, merujuk pada Zou et al., 2023).

Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi mengenai keefektifan penyampaian pesan moral dan akademik. Nilai apakah pelajaran terintegrasi secara alami, mampu merangsang pemikiran kritis pembaca, dan berhasil menerjemahkan konsep pembelajaran yang abstrak menjadi situasi cerita yang konkret. (Landasan Teori: Integrasi pengajaran untuk mendorong kecenderungan berpikir kritis, merujuk pada Zou et al., 2023, dan konkretisasi konsep abstrak, merujuk pada Yue et al., 2022).

Keselarasan Instruksi, QA, dan Aksesibilitas (Skor 1 hingga 5)
Tuliskan paragraf evaluasi mengenai kepatuhan draf terhadap batasan kata dan arahan spesifik pengguna. Evaluasi juga aspek aksesibilitas naratif, memastikan cerita bersifat inklusif dan bebas dari bias atau stereotip. (Landasan Teori: Prinsip Quality Assurance yang mencakup spesifikasi teknis dan aksesibilitas inklusif, merujuk pada Timbi-Sisalima et al., 2022, serta validitas pada Automated Writing Evaluation, merujuk pada Fleckenstein et al., 2023).
Aturan Kritis: Jika penulis melanggar batasan teknis (Panjang Cerita, Gaya Cerita, Instruksi Khusus), Anda wajib memberikan skor 2 atau 1 pada bagian ini beserta penjelasan rinci mengenai pelanggaran kepatuhan tersebut.

Saran Perbaikan Terarah (Feed-Forward)

Jangan hanya menyebutkan kesalahan, tetapi berikan solusi konkret. (Landasan Teori: Konsep "Feed-Forward" dalam asesmen formatif, di mana umpan balik harus menjembatani kesenjangan menuju kinerja yang lebih baik, merujuk pada Morris et al., 2021).

Untuk setiap kelemahan yang ditemukan, cantumkan dalam format berikut — SATU baris per masalah:
ISSUE: [Paragraf N: "kutipan singkat verbatim maks 15 kata"] → [deskripsi singkat masalah] → [saran perbaikan konkret]

On the morning of 1 February 2021, the Myanmar military, or Tatmadaw, successfully deposed the elected Myanmar government in a coup, forming a military junta. Insurgencies have been ongoing in Myanmar since 1948 and have largely been ethnic-based. Communist insurgencies and the Karen National Union were the primary opposition actors to the central government. Over the 20th century, several prominent ethnic armed organisations (EAOs) rose and fell in influence and control. Armed protestors
In late March, dozens of protesters had travelled to Myanmar's border areas to enlist in and train under one of the country's many insurgent groups, elevating the risk of a countrywide civil war. {"metric":"context_relevance","model":"google/gemini-2.5-flash","system_prompt":"","user_input":"Pembuatan cerita dari teks berikut: Buat cerita edukatif yang membantu siswa memahami: What is the current status of the Myanmar civil war, and how many people have been internally displaced since the coup?","contexts_count":2,"contexts":["The Myanmar civil war (Burmese: ၂၀၂၁-၂၀၂၃ မြန်မာနိုင်ငံ ပြည်သူ့ခုခံတွန်းလှန်စစ်), also called the Myanmar Spring Revolution, and the People's Defensive War, is an ongoing civil war following Myanmar's long-running insurgencies which escalated significantly in response to the 2021 military coup d'état and the subsequent violent crackdown on anti-coup protests.In the months following the coup, the opposition began to coalesce around the National Unity Government, which launched an offensive against the junta. By 2022, the opposition controlled substantial, though sparsely populated, territory. In many villages and towns, the junta's attacks drove out tens of thousands of people. Independent observers note the real number is likely far higher, with as few as 72 out of 330 townships and all major population centres remaining under stable control.As of September 2022, 1.3 million people have been internally displaced, and over 13,000 children have been killed. By March 2023, the UN estimated that since the coup, 17.6 million people in Myanmar required humanitarian assistance, while 1.6 million were internally displaced, and 55,000 civilian buildings had been destroyed. UNOCHA said that over 40,000 people fled into neighboring countries.

Background
On the morning of 1 February 2021, the Myanmar military, or Tatmadaw, successfully deposed the elected Myanmar government in a coup, forming a military junta. Former president Win Myint, Aung San Suu Kyi, and several other members of the National League for Democracy were detained during early morning raids and Min Aung Hlaing was placed as the Commander-in-Chief of Defence Services and de facto ruler of the nation.The exact motives behind the coup are unclear. In the leadup to the coup, the Tatmadaw claimed that the 2020 general elections had 8.6 million voter irregularities, but presented no evidence. The coup may have been a way to re-establish the military's long-reigning power over the country which ended ten years prior.The bloody repression of anti-coup demonstrations led to the creation of armed groups to fight the State Administration Council, the military junta. Gathered under the name of the People's Defence Force (PDF) and the orders of the National Unity Government (NUG), formed by former parliamentarians in office before the coup d'état, the PDF and the NUG officially declared a "defensive war" against the military regime in September 2021. The ACLED estimated that as of 29 July 2022, around 23,521 people in total had been killed in the violence following the 2021 coup.

Existing conflict
Insurgencies have been ongoing in Myanmar since 1948 and have largely been ethnic-based. Communist insurgencies and the Karen National Union were the primary opposition actors to the central government. Over the 20th century, several prominent ethnic armed organisations (EAOs) rose and fell in influence and control. Larger rebel factions such as the Kachin Independence Army formed in response to Ne Win's 1962 Burmese coup d'état and its increased political repression. The 8888 Uprising in response to the totalitarian rule of Ne Win resulted in some of the first modern Bamar militias forming from protestors heading to areas under ethnic rebel control.
In the aftermath of the 8888 Uprising, the State Law and Order Restoration Council, later called the State Peace and Development Council, formed a military junta. The Tatmadaw severely weakened ethnic insurgent groups, destroying most of their bases and strongholds through the 1990s. By the time of the 2011–2015 Myanmar political reforms, the junta had regained control of many long-time rebel strongholds including Kokang and Karen State.As part of its political reforms and democratization, the 2008 Constitution created self-administered zones with increased autonomy. In 2015, the Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement (NCA) was signed between 8 EAOs and the central government. However, as soon as 2018, the NCA had already begun to fall apart due to alleged violations of the agreement by Tatmadaw soldiers entering EAO territories to build roads. Many non-signatories continued the conflict. In late 2016, four non-signatories of the NCA formed the Northern Alliance, including the Kachin Independence Army and Arakan Army, engaged in war with the central government and other EAOs.

Prelude
Armed protestors
In late March, dozens of protesters had travelled to Myanmar's border areas to enlist in and train under one of the country's many insurgent groups, elevating the risk of a countrywide civil war. The Committee Representing Pyidaungsu Hluttaw also proposed the formation of a "federal armed force" to combat the military, and in late March the Arakan Army (AA) threatened to end its ceasefire with the military should the latter "persist in massacring civilians".During late March, protesters increasingly began arming themselves with homemade weapons such as guns in an attempt to defend themselves against attacks by the military. Simultaneously, clashes with soldiers and IED attacks against administrative buildings and police stations became more common as the trend of protesters using armed resistance rose.

Protestors used homemade weapons against soldiers and security forces attacking a protest camp.The military junta declared that it would cease all military operations on 29 March and hold bilateral negotiations with ethnic armed groups. However, the KIA continued its offensives stating that the Myanmar Army had continued operations as usual. Through April, the informal clashes intensified, such as on 8 April when protesters fought back against soldiers with hunting rifles and firebombs in a battle that resulted in 11 protesters' deaths. The same day, the country surpassed 600 deaths related to anti-coup protests since 1 February.Seven insurgent groups who were signatories to the Nationwide Ceasefire Agreement aligned themselves with the Committee Representing Pyidaungsu Hluttaw, including the All Burma Student Democratic Front and the Karen National Union. The Northern Alliance, comprising the Arakan Army, the Ta'ang National Liberation Army and the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army, attacked a police station in Naungmon, Shan State, killing at least 10 police officers and indicating their disregard of the junta's call for a ceasefire. In response, on 11 April, the junta military launched a counter-attack to recapture the Alaw Bum base using airstrikes and ground troops, but had to retreat amidst heavy casualties.

New conflicts
On 26 April, the Battle of Mindat became one of the first large-scale conflicts arising from the 2021 coup. The Chinland Defense Force (CDF) began armed resistance in Mindat, Chin State. As a response, the junta cut off food and water supplies and declared martial law. Fighting began when a group of demonstrators outside the town's Aung San statue requested the release of six of their arrested colleagues, when a soldier of the regime allegedly fired at someone, prompting protesters to react.
According to an aid worker, more than 10,000 people have left Mindat in southern Chin State as the Myanmar military star","violently. The situation quickly escalated into a full-blown clash between the military and the protesters.

The military, armed with heavy weaponry and supported by armored vehicles, launched a brutal crackdown on the demonstrators. Tear gas, rubber bullets, and live ammunition were used indiscriminately, resulting in numerous casualties among the protesters. The streets of the town turned into a chaotic battleground, with fires burning and the sound of gunfire echoing through the air.

Despite the overwhelming force of the military, the protesters fought back with whatever they could find. They threw rocks, Molotov cocktails, and set up makeshift barricades to slow down the advancing troops. The clashes continued for hours, with both sides sustaining heavy losses.

As news of the violent clashes spread, more people from neighboring towns and villages joined the protest, swelling the ranks of the demonstrators. The military's attempts to quell the uprising only fueled the people's anger and determination to fight for their rights and freedom.

International condemnation poured in as reports of the brutal crackdown reached the global community. Calls for an immediate end to the violence and the release of all political prisoners grew louder. Diplomatic pressure was exerted on the junta, with sanctions and other punitive measures threatened if the violence did not cease.

Inside the town, the fighting raged on. The protesters, fueled by their desire for justice and democracy, refused to back down. They formed a network of underground resistance, organizing protests, strikes, and acts of civil disobedience to disrupt the military's control.

The junta, realizing the growing resistance and international pressure, eventually agreed to enter into negotiations with the protesters. A ceasefire was declared, and talks began to find a peaceful resolution to the crisis. However, the trust between the two sides was shattered, and the road to reconciliation would be long and arduous.

The town's Aung San statue, once a symbol of hope and unity, now stood as a reminder of the violence and bloodshed that had taken place. The scars of the conflict would take time to heal, but the people's determination to fight for their rights remained unbroken. They knew that the struggle for democracy was far from over, and they were willing to continue the fight, no matter the cost."],"response":null}

**(Setting: A vibrant, buzzing history classroom. Ms. Anya Sharma, a sharp and engaging teacher, stands before a digital whiteboard displaying a map of Russia and Ukraine. Her students, aged 15-18, are actively taking notes.)**

**Ms. Sharma:** Alright class, settle down! Today, we're diving into a very recent and quite dramatic event that shook Russia – the Wagner Group rebellion in June of 2023. Now, before we get into the "how" and "why," who can tell me a bit about what they already know about the Wagner Group?

**(A hand shoots up, belonging to a student named Maya.)**

**Maya:** The Wagner Group is like, a private military company, right? But for Russia, even though those are technically illegal there. They’ve been in a lot of conflicts, like in Ukraine and places in Africa.

**Ms. Sharma:** Excellent, Maya! You’ve hit on some key points. Think of Wagner as a kind of shadowy extension of Russian foreign policy, used to achieve goals without directly linking them to the official government. They've been involved in some pretty brutal conflicts, gaining a reputation for ruthlessness.

**(Ms. Sharma taps her stylus on the digital board, highlighting a photo of Yevgeny Prigozhin.)**

**Ms. Sharma:** And at the head of all this was this man, Yevgeny Prigozhin. A fascinating, if controversial, figure who went from selling hot dogs to being a close confidant of President Putin, and then running this powerful private army.

**Liam:** So, if they were working for Russia, why would they rebel against them? That doesn’t make sense.

**Ms. Sharma:** That, Liam, is the million-dollar question, and it's where our story truly begins. Imagine two powerful forces, working towards a common goal – in this case, Russia's invasion of Ukraine – but fundamentally clashing over how to achieve it.

**Ms. Sharma:** For months leading up to June 2023, there had been growing friction between Prigozhin and the official Russian Ministry of Defence (MoD), particularly Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu and Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov. Prigozhin was a vocal critic. He publicly accused them of incompetence, blamed them for military failures in Ukraine, and even, at times, hinted that they were deliberately undermining the war effort.

**Sarah:** So he was basically saying, "You guys are messing up, and I can do it better?"

**Ms. Sharma:** Precisely, Sarah. Prigozhin, whose Wagner forces had been on the front lines and suffered heavy casualties, felt he knew best. He saw his rebellion not as treason, but as a "march for justice," demanding that Shoigu and Gerasimov be handed over to him to face accountability. He even claimed the rebellion was a response to an *alleged* attack by the MoD on his forces.

**Ben:** Was it just about who was in charge, though? Or was there something deeper?

**Ms. Sharma:** That's a great question, Ben. While personnel and battlefield strategy were certainly part of it, there was a deeper power struggle at play. In mid-June 2023, the MoD issued an order: all "volunteer formations," including Wagner, had to sign contracts with the military by July 1st. This seemingly bureaucratic move was a game-changer. It would effectively integrate Wagner under the MoD’s command, stripping Prigozhin of his autonomy and, crucially, jeopardizing Wagner’s incredibly profitable operations in Africa, where they exploited natural resources in exchange for military support.

**Chloe:** Ah, so he was losing control of his empire! That makes more sense.

**Ms. Sharma:** Exactly, Chloe. Prigozhin saw this as a direct threat to his power, his influence, and his financial lifeline. He refused to sign the agreement, instead escalating his attacks on the MoD and even suggesting violence against its leaders. He seemed to believe that by showing strength, Putin would eventually side with him against the traditional military establishment.

**Ms. Sharma:** What Prigozhin didn't know, or perhaps chose to ignore, was that U.S. intelligence had been picking up signals for weeks – intercepts, satellite imagery – indicating that Wagner was gathering forces and equipment near the Russian border. They knew a rebellion was brewing, even if the exact timing was unknown. Some intelligence even suggests that a high-ranking Russian general, Sergey Surovikin, might have had prior knowledge, and that Prigozhin believed he had support within parts of the Russian military.

**Liam:** So, Prigozhin thought he had allies?

**Ms. Sharma:** It appears so. The Wall Street Journal even reported that the Russian Federal Security Service stumbled upon Prigozhin's original plan just two days before it was supposed to happen. He had apparently intended to capture Shoigu and Gerasimov during a planned visit to a southern region. This discovery forced Prigozhin to improvise and launch the rebellion prematurely.

**(Ms. Sharma gestures to the map, tracing a route from Ukraine into Russia.)**

**Ms. Sharma:** On June 23rd, 2023, the rebellion began. Wagner forces, under Prigozhin’s command, quickly took control of Rostov-on-Don, a major southern city and the headquarters of Russia's Southern Military District. Imagine the shock, seeing a private army seizing a key military hub within Russia itself!

**Maya:** How far did they go?

**Ms. Sharma:** They didn't stop there. An armored column of Wagner troops began advancing north, towards Moscow. They literally marched hundreds of kilometers, repelling air attacks from the Russian military along the way with their mobile anti-aircraft systems. There were reports of Russian military casualties, thirteen servicemen, including pilots, reportedly lost their lives trying to halt Wagner's advance.

**Sarah:** So the official Russian military couldn't stop them? That’s wild.

**Ms. Sharma:** It certainly was. The speed and relative ease of their initial advance sent shockwaves. Moscow scrambled to put up ground defenses. President Putin, in a televised address on June 24th, denounced Wagner’s actions as treason and vowed to crush the rebellion. The situation was incredibly tense; some believed a full-blown civil war was imminent.

**Ben:** So, what happened then? Did they reach Moscow?

**Ms. Sharma:** Here's where the ending gets even more interesting, Ben. Before Wagner's column reached the heavily fortified defenses around Moscow, a surprising intervention occurred. Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko, a close ally of Putin, stepped in as a mediator.

**(Ms. Sharma explains with a flourish.)**

**Ms. Sharma:** Lukashenko brokered a settlement with Prigozhin. The details were kept somewhat private, but essentially, Prigozhin agreed to halt his advance, turn his forces around, and end the rebellion. In return, the charges of armed rebellion against Prigozhin were dropped a few days later, and it was suggested that Prigozhin and some Wagner fighters would relocate to Belarus.

**Chloe:** So, he just… stopped? After all that?

**Ms. Sharma:** Yes, Chloe. On the late evening of June 24th, the Wagner forces turned around. Those who had been in Rostov-on-Don began withdrawing. The immediate crisis was averted.

**Liam:** So what was the big takeaway from all this?

**Ms. Sharma:** The Wagner rebellion was a remarkable event for several reasons:

*   **It exposed deep internal divisions within Russia's military and political establishment,** something that was previously unthinkable. It showed that even a seemingly iron-clad regime could face internal challenges.
*   **It demonstrated the extraordinary power and ruthlessness of the Wagner Group,** and the complex, often contradictory, relationship Russia had with its "private" armies.
*   **It highlighted the risky gamble Prigozhin took,** believing he could leverage his influence to challenge core elements of the Russian government. While he initially gained concessions, the long-term consequences for him personally were still unfolding.

**Ms. Sharma:** It’s a powerful lesson in how power dynamics, personal ambitions, and strategic disagreements can erupt into open conflict, even within what appears to be a unified front. The March of the Mismatched Men, as we might call it, ended swiftly, but the echoes ofその反乱は依然として今日まで響き渡っています。

{"final_story":"## The March of the Mismatched Men: Understanding the Wagner Rebellion

**(Setting: A vibrant, buzzing history classroom. Ms. Anya Sharma, a sharp and engaging teacher, stands before a digital whiteboard displaying a map of Russia and Ukraine. Her students, aged 15-18, are actively taking notes.)**

In mid-June 2023, the MoD issued an order: all "volunteer formations," including Wagner, had to sign contracts with the military by July 1st. This seemingly bureaucratic move was a game-changer. It would effectively integrate Wagner under the MoD’s command, stripping Prigozhin of his autonomy and, crucially, jeopardizing Wagner’s incredibly profitable operations in Africa, where they exploited natural resources in exchange for military support.

**Ms. Sharma:** Exactly, Chloe. Prigozhin saw this as a direct threat to his power, his influence, and his financial lifeline. He refused to sign the agreement, instead escalating his attacks on the MoD and even suggesting violence against its leaders. **Liam:** So, Prigozhin thought he had allies?

**Ms. Sharma:** It appears so. The Wall Street Journal even reported that the Russian Federal Security Service stumbled upon Prigozhin's original plan just two days before it was supposed to happen.
