## Misi "Benteng Pelindung": Kisah Para Arsitek Kesehatan Global

**Prolog: Bayangan di Cakrawala**

Tahun 2045. Dunia telah pulih dari masa-masa sulit, meninggalkan bayangan pandemi COVID-19 sebagai pengingat pahit. Remaja bernama Arya, seorang siswa SMA yang cerdas dan penuh rasa ingin tahu, melenggang di koridor sekolah. Hari ini, pelajaran Biologi akan membahas sesuatu yang sangat dekat dengan sejarah modern: *Pencegahan Pandemi*.

Di depan kelas, Bu Ratna, guru Biologi mereka yang inspiratif, memulai pelajaran dengan sebuah pertanyaan yang membuat semua siswa berpikir: "Apa perbedaan antara *pencegahan* pandemi dan *mitigasi* pandemi?"

Hening sesaat. Beberapa siswa mulai berbisik, mencoba mengingat pelajaran sebelumnya.

"Bayangkan ini," Bu Ratna melanjutkan, "Jika rumahmu terbakar, *mitigasi* adalah memadamkan api, membangun kembali, dan memastikan kerusakan tidak terlalu parah. Tapi *pencegahan*, itu tentang memastikan percikan api tidak pernah menyentuh rumahmu sejak awal. Kita akan fokus pada itu hari ini: **bagaimana kita mencegah agar 'percikan api' penyakit menular tidak pernah menjadi 'kebakaran' besar yang tak terkendali.**"

Arya merasa tertantang. Dia selalu berpikir pencegahan itu hanya tentang cuci tangan dan masker, tapi Bu Ratna membuatnya terdengar jauh lebih kompleks dan mendalam.

**Bab 1: Jaring-Jaring Deteksi Dini**

"Coba kita tengok kasus SARS tahun 2002-2004," Bu Ratna memulai, menayangkan grafik. "Virus SARS-CoV-1 memiliki potensi mematikan. Tapi, dunia berhasil mencegahnya menjadi pandemi global. Mengapa?"

Seorang siswi bernama Lia, yang gemar membaca berita kesehatan, mengangkat tangan. "Karena respons cepat dari otoritas kesehatan, Bu! WHO dan negara-negara bekerja sama untuk melacak kasus dan mengisolasi penderita."

"Tepat sekali, Lia!" Bu Ratna tersenyum. "Ini adalah inti dari **infrastruktur dan pengembangan internasional** yang kuat. Bayangkan sistem kesehatan di seluruh dunia sebagai sebuah jaring laba-laba raksasa. Semakin kuat dan terhubung jaring itu, semakin cepat kita bisa merasakan getaran kecil – yaitu *outbreak* lokal – sebelum getaran itu mengguncang seluruh jaring."

Bu Ratna menampilkan peta dunia dengan titik-titik hijau yang terhubung garis. "Artinya, setiap negara, bahkan yang paling terpencil sekalipun, perlu memiliki:
1.  **Sistem pengawasan aktif (Active Surveillance):** Mampu mendeteksi secara dini kasus-kasus yang tidak biasa, seperti demam pneumonia atipikal.
2.  **Kapasitas koordinasi layanan kesehatan:** Mampu dengan cepat mengisolasi pasien, melacak kontak, dan memberikan perawatan.
3.  **Pertukaran informasi yang cepat dan transparan:** Tidak ada birokrasi bertele-tele yang menunda informasi penting.

"Pentingnya ini kadang terabaikan," Bu Ratna menambahkan. "Para peneliti di Afrika, Asia, atau Amerika Latin seringkali menjadi yang pertama melihat pola penyakit aneh, tapi mereka mungkin kekurangan fasilitas laboratorium untuk identifikasi lebih lanjut. Kita perlu memprioritaskan penelitian yang relevan dengan wilayah ini, memastikan diagnosis dan vaksin dapat diakses tanpa perlu pendingin yang canggih."

Arya membayangkan dokter-dokter pahlawan di desa terpencil, berusaha memecahkan teka-teki kesehatan tanpa banyak alat. "Jadi, intinya, kita harus membangun benteng dari pondasi yang paling rapuh sekalipun, Bu?" tanyanya.

"Persis!" Bu Ratna mengangguk. "Benteng itu harus kokoh di setiap sudutnya."

**Bab 2: Teknologi sebagai Tameng Pelindung**

"Sekarang, mari kita bicara tentang **langkah-langkah berbasis teknologi**," Bu Ratna beralih ke slide lain yang menampilkan gambar laboratorium canggih. "Ini adalah garis pertahanan kedua kita: Biosafety dan Regulasi Bioteknologi."

"Apa itu biosafety, Bu?" tanya Budi, siswa yang suka teknologi.

"Biosafety adalah praktik dan prosedur yang dirancang untuk mencegah paparan terhadap agen biologis berbahaya dan pelepasan yang tidak disengaja," jelas Bu Ratna. "Bayangkan laboratorium adalah medan perang mini. Kita harus memastikan semua senjata biologis (mikroorganisme) tetap terkunci dan terkendali. Ini meliputi:
1.  **Pembatasan penelitian agen biologis yang sangat menular:** Hanya peneliti terlatih di lingkungan yang sangat aman (Biosafety Level, BSL) yang diizinkan menangani agen berbahaya. Contohnya, virus seperti SARS-CoV-2 awalnya direkomendasikan ditangani pada BSL-3, bukan BSL-2 seperti virus-virus korona lainnya sebelumnya.
2.  **Peningkatan keamanan fisik dan edukasi ilmuwan:** Mencegah penyalahgunaan dan kecelakaan laboratorium.
3.  **Proses tinjauan yang ketat:** Memastikan risiko dijustifikasi dan diminimalkan, misalnya dalam penelitian *gain-of-function*."

Arya mengerutkan kening. "Apa itu *gain-of-function*, Bu? Terdengar seperti kita bermain-main dengan api."

"Pertanyaan bagus, Arya. *Gain-of-function* adalah penelitian yang bertujuan untuk memodifikasi agen biologis agar memperoleh atau meningkatkan fungsi tertentu, misalnya menjadi lebih menular atau lebih mematikan. Ada perdebatan besar mengenai penelitian ini," Bu Ratna menjelaskan. "Para pendukung mengatakan ini bisa membantu kita membuat vaksin dan terapi antisipatif. Namun, para kritikus khawatir risiko kebocoran atau kesalahan bisa memicu pandemi baru. Ini adalah tantangan besar: bagaimana kita menyeimbangkan kebutuhan akan ilmu pengetahuan dengan risiko yang melekat?"

"Jadi, *gain-of-function* itu seperti membuat mutan di laboratorium?" tanya Budi, sedikit terkejut.

"Dalam arti tertentu, ya, Budi. Dan itu sebabnya **memantau dan memperkuat protokol laboratorium di seluruh dunia** itu krusial. Tidak ada satu pun negara atau lab yang boleh menanggung risiko ini sendirian tanpa pengawasan global," tegas Bu Ratna.

Dia kemudian menampilkan gambar penjelajah di hutan, mengambil sampel dari kelelawar. "Tak hanya di laboratorium, **protokol kerja lapangan** juga sangat penting. Pengambilan sampel satwa liar, misalnya. Kita mencari virus di habitat aslinya. Meskipun berisiko, upaya ini membantu kita mengidentifikasi potensi ancaman *zoonotic spillover* – perpindahan virus dari hewan ke manusia. Ingat kasus NeoCoV yang ditemukan di kelelawar? Studi seperti itu mengingatkan kita untuk tetap waspada."

"Tapi bukankah itu sendiri berisiko, Bu?" tanya Lia. "Jika kita mengganggu habitat atau membawa virus pulang?"

"Itu adalah dilema besar, Lia," jawab Bu Ratna serius. "Beberapa ahli memang berpendapat demikian. Namun, jika kita tidak melakukan sampling sama sekali, kita akan buta terhadap virus-virus baru yang berpotensi memicu pandemi di masa depan. Kuncinya adalah melakukannya dengan standar biosafety tertinggi dan protokol yang sangat ketat, seperti yang dilakukan di Laos saat menemukan kerabat SARS-CoV-2 di kelelawar, atau studi di Wuhan yang menemukan bahwa sample di sekitar Wuhan saat awal COVID-19 muncul tidak menemukan virus tersebut pada hewan liar. Kita harus terus meneliti, namun dengan sangat hati-hati, dengan ukuran sampel yang besar untuk kesimpulan yang lebih akurat."

**Bab 3: Deteksi Dini, Reaksi Cepat, dan Vaksinasi Cincin**

"Lalu, ada kasus cacar monyet pada tahun 2022," Bu Ratna beralih ke kasus konkret lainnya. "Kasus ini menunjukkan pentingnya **deteksi dini dan respons cepat** bahkan untuk penyakit yang kita kira sudah kita pahami."

Dia menjelaskan bagaimana WHO melaporkan lonjakan kasus di negara-negara yang tidak endemik. "Metode utama yang digunakan untuk membendung penyebaran awal adalah 'vaksinasi cincin' (*ring vaccination*). Ada yang tahu apa itu?"

Arya mengangkat tangan lagi. "Apakah itu artinya orang-orang yang kontak dekat dengan kasus positif divaksin, Bu? Seperti membentuk cincin pelindung di sekitar orang yang sakit?"

"Tepat sekali, Arya! Dan ini dikoordinasikan dengan vaksinasi pra-paparan untuk kelompok berisiko tinggi. Ini menunjukkan bahwa bahkan dengan infrastruktur yang kuat dan teknologi biosafety, kita tetap membutuhkan **strategi respons lapangan yang efektif dan teruji**."

**Epilog: Arsitek Masa Depan**

Bu Ratna memberikan senyum hangat kepada siswanya. "Kalian melihatnya sekarang? Pencegahan pandemi bukanlah tentang satu atau dua solusi sederhana. Ini adalah sebuah misi kompleks yang melibatkan:
*   Membangun **infrastruktur kesehatan global yang tangguh** dan saling terhubung.
*   Mengembangkan dan menerapkan **teknologi biosafety yang canggih dan regulasi yang ketat** di laboratorium dan lapangan.
*   Menerapkan **strategi deteksi dini dan respons cepat** seperti vaksinasi cincin.
*   Yang terpenting, ini membutuhkan **kolaborasi internasional yang kuat dan tanpa henti**, menyingkirkan ego dan kepentingan nasional demi kesehatan umat manusia."

Dia melirik Arya. "Beberapa ahli bahkan berpendapat, usaha pencegahan pandemi itu sendiri bisa berisiko, seperti pengambilan sampel virus di alam liar. Tapi tidak melakukan apa-apa juga sama berbahayanya. Ini adalah keseimbangan yang sulit, sebuah area di mana kalian, generasi masa depan, mungkin akan menjadi para arsitek dan penjaga benteng pelindung dunia."

Arya menatap Bu Ratna, kemudian ke arah teman-temannya. Dia tidak lagi melihat pencegahan pandemi sebagai hal sepele. Itu adalah perjuangan tanpa akhir, sebuah pertahanan global yang membutuhkan kecerdasan, keberanian, dan kerja sama setiap orang.

Di luar jendela kelas, matahari bersinar terang. Arya merasa ada tanggung jawab baru yang diemban di pundaknya. Masa depan kesehatan global akan bergantung pada bagaimana generasi mereka memahami dan bertindak atas pelajaran ini. Dia tahu, membangun benteng pelindung agar "percikan api" tidak pernah menjadi "kebakaran" besar adalah misi terpenting yang harus terus diperjuangkan.

Tapi *pencegahan*, itu tentang memastikan percikan api tidak pernah menyentuh rumahmu sejak awal. Kita akan fokus pada itu hari ini: **bagaimana kita mencegah agar 'percikan api' penyakit menular tidak pernah menjadi 'kebakaran' besar yang tak terkendali.**"

Arya merasa tertantang. Dia selalu berpikir pencegahan itu hanya tentang cuci tangan dan masker, tapi Bu Ratna membuatnya terdengar jauh lebih kompleks dan mendalam.

"Coba kita tengok kasus SARS tahun 2002-2004," Bu Ratna memulai, menayangkan grafik. "Virus SARS-CoV-1 memiliki potensi mematikan. Tapi, dunia berhasil mencegahnya menjadi pandemi global. Mengapa?"

Seorang siswi bernama Lia, yang gemar membaca berita kesehatan, mengangkat tangan. "Karena respons cepat dari otoritas kesehatan, Bu! WHO dan negara-negara bekerja sama untuk melacak kasus dan mengisolasi penderita."

"Tepat sekali, Lia!" Bu Ratna tersenyum. "Ini adalah inti dari **infrastruktur dan pengembangan internasional** yang kuat. Bayangkan sistem kesehatan di seluruh dunia sebagai sebuah jaring laba-laba raksasa. Semakin kuat dan terhubung jaring itu, semakin cepat kita bisa merasakan getaran kecil – yaitu *outbreak* lokal – sebelum getaran itu mengguncang seluruh jaring."

2.  **Peningkatan keamanan fisik dan edukasi ilmuwan:** Mencegah penyalahgunaan dan kecelakaan laboratorium.
3.  **Proses tinjauan yang ketat:** Memastikan risiko dijustifikasi dan diminimalkan, misalnya dalam penelitian *gain-of-function*."

"Itu adalah dilema besar, Lia," jawab Bu Ratna serius. "Beberapa ahli memang berpendapat demikian. Kuncinya adalah melakukannya dengan standar biosafety tertinggi dan protokol yang sangat ketat, seperti yang dilakukan di Laos saat menemukan kerabat SARS-CoV-2 di kelelawar, atau studi di Wuhan yang menemukan bahwa sample di sekitar Wuhan saat awal COVID-19 muncul tidak menemukan virus tersebut pada hewan liar. Kita harus terus meneliti, namun dengan sangat hati-hati, dengan ukuran sampel yang besar untuk kesimpulan yang lebih akurat."

"Lalu, ada kasus cacar monyet pada tahun 2022," Bu Ratna beralih ke kasus konkret lainnya. "Kasus ini menunjukkan pentingnya **deteksi dini dan respons cepat** bahkan untuk penyakit yang kita kira sudah kita pahami."

Those include measures to reduce causes of new infectious diseases and measures to prevent outbreaks and epidemics from becoming pandemics.
It is not to be mistaken for pandemic preparedness or mitigation (e.g. against COVID-19) which largely seek to mitigate the magnitude of negative effects of pandemics, although the topics may overlap with pandemic prevention in some respects.
Some biosafety and public health researchers contend that certain pandemic prevention efforts themselves carry risk of triggering pandemics (e.g. wildlife virus sampling), though not engaging in any form of sampling also carries the risk of being unprepared for future spillover events and being unaware of future pandemic pathogens.

History
2002–2004 SARS outbreak
During the 2002–2004 SARS outbreak, the SARS-CoV-1 virus was prevented from causing a pandemic of Severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS). Rapid action by national and international health authorities such as the World Health Organization helped to slow transmission and eventually broke the chain of transmission, which ended the localized epidemics before they could become a pandemic. Human-to-human transmission of SARS may be considered eradicated, however, it could re-emerge as SARS-CoV-1 probably persists as a potential zoonotic threat in its original animal reservoir. This warrants monitoring and reporting of suspicious cases of atypical pneumonia. Effective isolation of patients was enough to control spread because infected individuals usually do not transmit the virus until several days after symptoms begin and are most infectious only after developing severe symptoms.

MERS-CoV/NeoCoV alert
In January 2022, Chinese scientists at the Wuhan University and other institutions reported in a preprint the detection of the closest MERS-CoV relative in bats to date, NeoCoV, and another virus, PDF-2180-CoV, that can efficiently use bats' ACE2 for cell entry. The study, now published in Nature found that one mutation could result in a theoretical 'MERS-CoV-2' that, like SARS-CoV-2, can use humans' ACE2 receptor. The theoretical virus could also have a high mortality burden, since MERS-CoV had a case fatality rate of around 35%. This 'MERS-CoV-2' therefore represents a risk to biosafety and potential zoonotic spillover. The study emphasized the need for pathogen/spillover surveillance to further understand any possible threat from related viruses. The WHO stated that further study is needed to find out "whether the virus detected in the study will pose a risk for humans".

Monkeypox
On 21 May 2022, the WHO reported on the international 2022 monkeypox outbreak in non-endemic countries which involved an unprecedented number of cases detected outside of Africa. The first of these cases was detected on 6 May 2022. The main method used for early containment (see below) is 'ring vaccination' – vaccinating close contacts of positive cases via already-existing vaccines alongside pre-exposure vaccination of members of the public at higher risk.

Measures
Infrastructure and international development
Robust, collaborating public health systems that have the capacity for active surveillance for early detection of cases and to mobilize their health care coordination capacity may be required to be able stop contagion promptly. After an outbreak there is a certain window of time during which a pandemic can still be stopped by the competent authorities isolating the first infected and/or fighting the pathogen. A good global infrastructure, consequent information exchange, minimal delays due to bureaucracy and effective, targeted treatment measures can be prepared. In 2012 it has been proposed to consider pandemic prevention as an aspect of international development in terms of health-care infrastructure and changes to the pathogen-related dynamics between humans and their environment including animals. Often local authority carers or doctors in Africa, Asia or Latin America register uncommon accumulations (or clusterings) of symptoms but lack options for more detailed investigations. Scientists state that "research relevant to countries with weaker surveillance, lab facilities and health systems should be prioritized" and that "in those regions, vaccine supply routes should not rely on refrigeration, and diagnostics should be available at the point of care". Two researchers have suggested that public health systems "in each country" need to be capable of detecting contagion early, diagnosing it accurately, implementing effective disease control measures, and fully collaborating with the relevant international authorities at each stage (see below). U.S. officials have proposed a range of reforms to international health regulations and global institutions for global health security. The "entire architecture of the response to epidemics" may need to get adapted, evolving "from crisis response during discrete outbreaks to an integrated cycle of preparation, response and recovery" (see also #International coordination).

Technology-centric measures
Biosafety technologies and biotechnology regulation
Potential policies that support global biosafety could make use of various technologies, including but not limited to laboratory containment technologies – for example, tools could promote compliance with existing and novel biosecurity norms and standards. Proposals to increase biosafety in terms of laboratories, scientific field work and research and development-related activities include:

limiting research on highly contagious biological agents to only trained researchers in well-protected environments and advanced biological safety systems and disposal of biohazards.
improving physical security and educating scientists about the misuse potentials
review processes that ensure risks are justified and minimized, such as preventing certain gain-of-function studies (the exact definition of "gain-of-function" is contested and there also the term "enhanced potential pandemic pathogens"). Arguments for gain-of-function-type research may include "that vaccines and therapeutics can be pre-emptively researched and developed" this way.
monitoring and strengthening laboratory protocols around the worldWork on coronaviruses at the Wuhan Institute of Virology was carried out at biosafety level 2 with level 4 being the most secure. Level 3 containment is now recommended for SARS-CoV-2. As of 2020, the CDC and other health agencies recommended handling non-SARS non-MERS human coronaviruses and SARS-related coronaviruses from wild animals at Biosafety Level 2 in vitro and Level 3 in vivo.
According to a study of Indian BSL-2 and BSL-3 facilities, "there are no national guidelines or reference standards available in India on certification and validation of biosafety laboratories"
In a 2018 study it was suggested that there is a need "to update international laboratory biosafety guidance" "to globalize biosafety"
In the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic there was a "global surge in labs that handle dangerous pathogens" and as of 2022 some researchers "are concerned about [these]".
monitoring and strengthening field work protocols around the world (such as viral sampling)The so far closest known relative virus (with a 96.8% similarity) to SARS-CoV-2 was found in samples from wild horseshoe bats in/at caves in northern Laos. No SARS-CoV-2 related viruses could be found in any samples collected in China, including from the only two domestic caves where RaTG13 and RmYN02 were detected, indicating such viruses may currently not circulate in bats in the country. A study of wild animals sampled in and around Wuhan at the beginning of COVID-19 emergence did not find SARS-CoV-2 or its progenitor virus in these samples. However, a virologist noted that their "sample sizes are not large enough" – 334 bats instead of "tens of thousands of bats". While another study claims to hav","to draw definitive conclusions. The study, published in the journal Nature, analyzed samples from over 12,000 animals, including bats, rodents, and other wildlife, collected from Hubei province between May 2019 and November 2020.

The researchers used various techniques to test the samples for the presence of coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2 and its closest known relatives. They found no evidence of SARS-CoV-2 or any closely related viruses in the samples.

However, the study's lead author, Dr. Peter Daszak, acknowledged that the sample sizes were relatively small, particularly for bats. He stated that they tested 334 bats, which is a significant number compared to previous studies, but still not large enough to draw definitive conclusions.

Dr. Daszak emphasized the need for larger-scale surveillance efforts to better understand the diversity and prevalence of coronaviruses in wildlife populations. He suggested that tens of thousands of bats should be sampled to get a more accurate picture of the viruses circulating in these animals.

The study also highlighted the importance of continued monitoring of wildlife populations for emerging viruses. It is crucial to understand the potential sources of zoonotic diseases like COVID-19 to prevent future outbreaks.

Overall, while this study did not find SARS-CoV-2 or its progenitor virus in the sampled animals, further research with larger sample sizes is needed to fully understand the origins of the virus and its transmission to humans."],"response":null}

Veronica, seorang siswi SMA pecinta sains, duduk di kursinya dengan mata berbinar. Di layar depan, presentasi geologi planetarium menunjukkan gambar planet Venus yang diselimuti awan tebal. Veronica sudah tahu Venus panas, tapi ia tidak menyangka presentasi Dr. Arya akan membawanya pada topik yang sangat ia gemari: vulkanisme. "Tahukah kalian," Dr. Arya melanjutkan, "permukaan Venus didominasi oleh fitur-fitur vulkanik. Bayangkan, ada lebih dari 80.000 gunung berapi di Venus! Jauh lebih banyak dari planet lain."

Veronica mencatat dengan antusias. "Dan yang lebih menarik," kata Dr. Arya, "sekitar 65% permukaan Venus terdiri dari dataran lava vulkanik, menunjukkan bahwa gunung berapi telah membentuk permukaannya secara masif."

**Perdebatan Aktivitas Vulkanik: Kilas Balik dan Bukti Terbaru**

"Selama bertahun-tahun, ilmuwan berdebat: apakah gunung berapi di Venus masih aktif, atau hanya sisa-sisa masa lalu?" Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar permukaan Venus dengan beberapa kawah. "Jumlah kawah tumbukan yang sedikit di permukaan Venus sebenarnya indikasi adanya pembaharuan permukaan yang relatif baru. Kemungkinan besar, banjir lava yang menyelimuti planet ini adalah penyebabnya."

Veronica teringat pelajaran tentang kawah tumbukan di Bumi. Jika ada aktivitas geologi, kawah-kawah lama akan tertutup.

Veronica merasa seperti menjadi bagian dari penemuan ilmiah itu. "Jadi, benar-benar aktif, ya, Dok?" tanyanya.

"Betul sekali, Veronica!" Dr. Arya tersenyum. "Ini adalah terobosan besar dalam memahami evolusi Venus."

**Jenis-Jenis Gunung Berapi di Venus: Kembaran yang Berbeda**

"Sekarang, mari kita bicara tentang jenis-jenis gunung berapi di Venus," kata Dr. Arya. "Di Bumi, kita punya gunung berapi perisai seperti di Hawaii, dan stratovolcano atau komposit seperti Gunung St. Helens. Nah, di Venus, sebagian besar adalah gunung berapi perisai juga."

Veronica mengangkat tangan. "Tapi bedanya apa, Dok?"

"Pertanyaan bagus, Veronica!" Dr. Arya mengangguk. "Di Bumi, gunung berapi perisai seperti Mauna Kea bisa sangat tinggi, puluhan kilometer lebar dan hingga 10 km tingginya jika diukur dari dasar laut. Lava mereka relatif encer, memungkinkan gas mudah keluar. Stratovolcano, di sisi lain, terkait dengan lempeng tektonik. Ketika kerak samudera menyelip ke bawah kerak lain, bersama dengan air laut, menghasilkan lava yang lebih kental, yang seringkali meletus dengan lebih dahsyat karena gas terperangkap."

"Nah, di Venus," Dr. Arya melanjutkan, "tidak ada lempeng tektonik atau air laut. Jadi, sebagian besar gunung berapi adalah tipe perisai. Namun, bentuknya berbeda! Meskipun bisa menutupi area ratusan kilometer, gunung berapi perisai Venus relatif datar, dengan tinggi rata-rata hanya 1,5 km. Kenapa? Karena gravitasi Venus dan tekanan atmosfer yang sangat tinggi membuat lava menyebar lebih luas dan membentuk struktur yang lebih rendah."

**Keunikan Venus: Si Pancake dan Si Kutu Raksasa**

"Tapi, ada juga jenis gunung berapi yang unik di Venus, yang tidak kita temukan di Bumi," Dr. Arya melanjutkan dengan semangat. "Pertama, ada yang disebut **kubah pancake**."

Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar kubah-kubah besar yang terlihat seperti tumpukan pancake raksasa. "Kubah-kubah ini bisa berdiameter hingga 15 km dan tingginya kurang dari 1 km. Mereka seratus kali lebih besar dari kubah lava di Bumi! Mereka terbentuk oleh lava yang sangat kental, kaya silika, yang meletus di bawah tekanan atmosfer Venus yang sangat tinggi."

Veronica terkesima. **Kubah pancake**! Nama itu sendiri sudah menarik.

"Kedua, ada struktur yang kami sebut 'kutu' atau **scalloped margin domes**," lanjut Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar kubah dengan 'kaki-kaki' yang tidak beraturan. "Mereka terlihat seperti kutu raksasa karena memiliki banyak 'kaki' di sekelilingnya. Diyakini, 'kaki' ini terbentuk akibat peristiwa longsoran di tepiannya, dan kita sering melihat puing-puing berserakan di sekitarnya."

"Selain itu, ada juga fitur seperti **novae**," Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar pola retakan radial. "Ini adalah jaringan saluran magma atau graben yang memancar keluar. Terbentuk ketika sejumlah besar magma keluar ke permukaan, membentuk punggung dan parit radial yang sangat memantulkan radar."

"Terakhir, ada **arachnoids**," Dr. Arya menunjukkan gambar pola seperti jaring laba-laba. "Dinamai demikian karena bentuknya menyerupai jaring laba-laba, dengan beberapa oval konsentris yang dikelilingi oleh jaringan retakan radial yang kompleks, mirip **nova**. "Veronica, tahukah kamu mengapa kita belum bisa langsung melihat kilat di Venus?" Dr. Arya bertanya.

Veronica mengerutkan kening. "Karena awan tebalnya, Dok?"

"Tepat sekali!" Dr. Arya mengacungkan jempol. "Atmosfer Venus yang kaya karbon dioksida sangat padat, 90 kali lipat dari Bumi. Awan-awannya terbuat dari asam sulfat, yang menyerap dan menyebarkan cahaya, membuat kilatan petir sulit terlihat."

"Tapi, ada bukti tidak langsung bahwa petir mungkin terjadi di sana," Dr. Arya melanjutkan. "Misalnya, perubahan jumlah gas sulfur dioksida di atmosfer atas dapat menunjukkan aktivitas vulkanik. Letusan vulkanik dapat menghasilkan muatan listrik yang memicu petir."

"Juga, awan konvektif di Venus, yang terlihat seperti kembang kol dan bisa mencapai ketinggian 70 km, menunjukkan kemungkinan adanya konveksi atmosfer, proses yang di Bumi menghasilkan badai petir," jelas Dr. Arya. "Namun, upaya mendeteksi petir secara langsung dengan gelombang radio frekuensi sangat rendah (VLF) belum membuahkan hasil pasti."

"Misi-misi masa depan ke Venus, seperti VERITAS dan DAVINCI+ dari NASA, diharapkan bisa mengungkap misteri ini," Dr. Arya mengakhiri presentasinya. "Mereka akan mempelajari atmosfer dan permukaan Venus secara detail, mungkin akan menjawab pertanyaan tentang petir di sana."

Veronica sekarang memiliki gambaran yang jauh lebih jelas tentang Venus. Ia tidak hanya belajar tentang jenis-jenis gunung berapi yang unik di sana—kubah pancake dan 'kutu'—tetapi juga perbedaan mereka dengan gunung berapi Bumi, dipengaruhi oleh ketiadaan lempeng tektonik, tekanan atmosfer yang tinggi, dan komposisi lava. Ia juga memahami bagaimana misteri petir di Venus masih menunggu untuk dipecahkan. "Baiklah, para penjelajah ruang angkasa muda," suara mentor mereka, Dr. Arya, menggema. "Hari ini kita akan menjelajahi salah satu planet terpanas dan paling misterius di tata surya kita: Venus, si kembaran Bumi!"

Veronica sudah tahu Venus panas, tapi ia tidak menyangka presentasi Dr. Arya akan membawanya pada topik yang sangat ia gemari: vulkanisme. "Tahukah kalian," Dr. Arya melanjutkan, "permukaan Venus didominasi oleh fitur-fitur vulkanik. Bayangkan, ada lebih dari 80.000 gunung berapi di Venus! Jauh lebih banyak dari planet lain."

Veronica mencatat dengan antusias. "Dan yang lebih menarik," kata Dr. Arya, "sekitar 65% permukaan Venus terdiri dari dataran lava vulkanik, menunjukkan bahwa gunung berapi telah membentuk permukaannya secara masif."

**Perdebatan Aktivitas Vulkanik: Kilas Balik dan Bukti Terbaru**

"Selama bertahun-tahun, ilmuwan berdebat: apakah gunung berapi di Venus masih aktif, atau hanya sisa-sisa masa lalu?" Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar permukaan Venus dengan beberapa kawah. "Jumlah kawah tumbukan yang sedikit di permukaan Venus sebenarnya indikasi adanya pembaharuan permukaan yang relatif baru. Kemungkinan besar, banjir lava yang menyelimuti planet ini adalah penyebabnya."

Veronica teringat pelajaran tentang kawah tumbukan di Bumi. Jika ada aktivitas geologi, kawah-kawah lama akan tertutup.

"Penjajakan radar oleh wahana Magellan, bertahun-tahun yang lalu, telah menunjukkan bukti aktivitas vulkanik yang relatif baru," Dr. Arya melanjutkan. "Misalnya, di gunung berapi tertinggi Venus, Maat Mons, ditemukan aliran abu di dekat puncak. Tapi, sampai baru-baru ini, belum ada bukti langsung letusan. Namun, pada Januari 2020, beberapa studi menunjukkan bahwa Venus memang aktif secara vulkanis, meskipun tidak spesifik di Maat Mons. Dan yang paling menggembirakan, pada Maret 2023, ilmuwan mengumumkan **bukti langsung** aktivitas vulkanik! Mereka menemukan sebuah lubang ventilasi yang telah meluas secara signifikan dalam kurun waktu 8 bulan di wilayah Maat Mons, dari citra Magellan yang bahkan sudah berumur 30 tahun!"

Veronica merasa seperti menjadi bagian dari penemuan ilmiah itu. "Jadi, benar-benar aktif, ya, Dok?" tanyanya.

"Betul sekali, Veronica!" Dr. Arya tersenyum. "Ini adalah terobosan besar dalam memahami evolusi Venus."

**Jenis-Jenis Gunung Berapi di Venus: Kembaran yang Berbeda**

"Sekarang, mari kita bicara tentang jenis-jenis gunung berapi di Venus," kata Dr. Arya. "Di Bumi, kita punya gunung berapi perisai seperti di Hawaii, dan stratovolcano atau komposit seperti Gunung St. Helens. Nah, di Venus, sebagian besar adalah gunung berapi perisai juga."

Veronica mengangkat tangan. "Tapi bedanya apa, Dok?"

"Pertanyaan bagus, Veronica!" Dr. Arya mengangguk. "Di Bumi, gunung berapi perisai seperti Mauna Kea bisa sangat tinggi, puluhan kilometer lebar dan hingga 10 km tingginya jika diukur dari dasar laut. Lava mereka relatif encer, memungkinkan gas mudah keluar. Stratovolcano, di sisi lain, terkait dengan lempeng tektonik. Ketika kerak samudera menyelip ke bawah kerak lain, bersama dengan air laut, menghasilkan lava yang lebih kental, yang seringkali meletus dengan lebih dahsyat karena gas terperangkap."

"Nah, di Venus," Dr. Arya melanjutkan, "tidak ada lempeng tektonik atau air laut. Jadi, sebagian besar gunung berapi adalah tipe perisai. Namun, bentuknya berbeda! Meskipun bisa menutupi area ratusan kilometer, gunung berapi perisai Venus relatif datar, dengan tinggi rata-rata hanya 1,5 km. Kenapa? Karena gravitasi Venus dan tekanan atmosfer yang sangat tinggi membuat lava menyebar lebih luas dan membentuk struktur yang lebih rendah."

**Keunikan Venus: Si Pancake dan Si Kutu Raksasa**

"Tapi, ada juga jenis gunung berapi yang unik di Venus, yang tidak kita temukan di Bumi," Dr. Arya melanjutkan dengan semangat. "Pertama, ada yang disebut **kubah pancake**."

Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar kubah-kubah besar yang terlihat seperti tumpukan pancake raksasa. "Kubah-kubah ini bisa berdiameter hingga 15 km dan tingginya kurang dari 1 km. Mereka seratus kali lebih besar dari kubah lava di Bumi! Mereka terbentuk oleh lava yang sangat kental, kaya silika, yang meletus di bawah tekanan atmosfer Venus yang sangat tinggi."

Veronica terkesima. **Kubah pancake**! Nama itu sendiri sudah menarik.

"Kedua, ada struktur yang kami sebut 'kutu' atau **scalloped margin domes**," lanjut Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar kubah dengan 'kaki-kaki' yang tidak beraturan. "Mereka terlihat seperti kutu raksasa karena memiliki banyak 'kaki' di sekelilingnya. Diyakini, 'kaki' ini terbentuk akibat peristiwa longsoran di tepiannya, dan kita sering melihat puing-puing berserakan di sekitarnya."

"Selain itu, ada juga fitur seperti **novae**," Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar pola retakan radial. "Ini adalah jaringan saluran magma atau graben yang memancar keluar. Terbentuk ketika sejumlah besar magma keluar ke permukaan, membentuk punggung dan parit radial yang sangat memantulkan radar."

"Terakhir, ada **arachnoids**," Dr. Arya menunjukkan gambar pola seperti jaring laba-laba. "Dinamai demikian karena bentuknya menyerupai jaring laba-laba, dengan beberapa oval konsentris yang dikelilingi oleh jaringan retakan radial yang kompleks, mirip **nova**. Belum pasti apakah semua arachnoids memiliki asal yang sama atau hasil dari proses geologi yang berbeda."

"Veronica, tahukah kamu mengapa kita belum bisa langsung melihat kilat di Venus?" Dr. Arya bertanya.

Veronica mengerutkan kening. "Karena awan tebalnya, Dok?"

"Tepat sekali!" Dr. Arya mengacungkan jempol. "Atmosfer Venus yang kaya karbon dioksida sangat padat, 90 kali lipat dari Bumi. Awan-awannya terbuat dari asam sulfat, yang menyerap dan menyebarkan cahaya, membuat kilatan petir sulit terlihat."

"Tapi, ada bukti tidak langsung bahwa petir mungkin terjadi di sana," Dr. Arya melanjutkan. "Misalnya, perubahan jumlah gas sulfur dioksida di atmosfer atas dapat menunjukkan aktivitas vulkanik. Letusan vulkanik dapat menghasilkan muatan listrik yang memicu petir."

"Juga, awan konvektif di Venus, yang terlihat seperti kembang kol dan bisa mencapai ketinggian 70 km, menunjukkan kemungkinan adanya konveksi atmosfer, proses yang di Bumi menghasilkan badai petir," jelas Dr. Arya. "Namun, upaya mendeteksi petir secara langsung dengan gelombang radio frekuensi sangat rendah (VLF) belum membuahkan hasil pasti."

Ia juga memahami bagaimana misteri petir di Venus masih menunggu untuk dipecahkan. {"metric":"context_relevance","model":"google/gemini-2.5-flash","system_prompt":"","user_input":"Pembuatan cerita dari teks berikut: Buat cerita edukatif yang membantu siswa memahami: What types of volcanoes are found on Venus, and how do they differ from those on Earth?","contexts_count":2,"contexts":["The surface of Venus is dominated by volcanic features and has more volcanoes than any other planet in the Solar System. It has a surface that is 90% basalt, and about 65% of the planet consists of a mosaic of volcanic lava plains, indicating that volcanism played a major role in shaping its surface. There are more than 1,000 volcanic structures and possible periodic resurfacing of Venus by floods of lava. The planet may have had a major global resurfacing event about 500 million years ago, from what scientists can tell from the density of impact craters on the surface. Venus has an atmosphere rich in carbon dioxide, with a density that is 90 times that of Earth's atmosphere.
There are over 80,000 volcanoes on Venus detected through radar mapping. For many years scientists debated on whether Venus was currently active or if the volcanic structures were remnants from the past. There are few impact craters on Venus' surface which pointed to relatively recent resurfacing. The most likely resurfacing event would have been volcanic flows.  Radar sounding by the Magellan probe revealed evidence for comparatively recent volcanic activity at Venus's highest volcano Maat Mons, in the form of ash flows near the summit and on the northern flank. Although many lines of evidence such as this suggest that volcanoes on Venus have been recently active, present-day eruptions at Maat Mons have not been confirmed. Nevertheless, other more recent studies, in January 2020, suggest that Venus, though not Maat Mons specifically, is indeed currently volcanically active. In 2023, scientists reexamined topographical images of the Maat Mons region taken by the Magellan orbiter. Using computer simulations they determined that the topography had changed during an 8-month interval, and have concluded that active volcanism was the cause. Until 2023 there had only been hints of active volcanism; announced in March 2023 scientists imaged a vent expanding in Magellan images which is the proof needed to announce active volcanism

Types of volcanoes
Venus has shield volcanoes, widespread lava flows and some unusual volcanoes called pancake domes and "tick-like" structures which are not present on Earth. Pancake dome volcanoes are up to 15 km (9.3 mi) in diameter and less than 1 km (0.62 mi) in height and are 100 times larger than lava domes formed on Earth. They are usually associated with coronae and tesserae (large regions of highly deformed terrain, folded and fractured in two or three dimensions, which are unique to Venus). The pancakes are thought to be formed by highly viscous, silica-rich lava erupting under Venus's high atmospheric pressure.

The "tick-like" structures are called scalloped margin domes. They are commonly called ticks because they appear as domes with numerous legs. They are thought to have undergone mass wasting events such as landslides on their margins. Sometimes deposits of debris can be seen scattered around them.

On Earth, volcanoes are mainly of two types: shield volcanoes and composite or stratovolcanoes.  The shield volcanoes, for example those in Hawaii, eject magma from the depths of the Earth in zones called hot spots.  The lava from these volcanoes is relatively fluid and permits the escape of gases.  Composite volcanoes, such as Mount St. Helens and Mount Pinatubo, are associated with tectonic plates.  In this type of volcano, the oceanic crust of one plate is sliding underneath the other in a subduction zone, together with an inflow of seawater, producing a gummier lava that restricts the exit of the gases, and for that reason, composite volcanoes tend to erupt more violently.

On Venus, where there are no tectonic plates or seawater, volcanoes are mostly of the shield type. Nevertheless, the morphology of volcanoes on Venus is different: on Earth, shield volcanoes can be a few tens of kilometres wide and up to 10 km (6.2 mi) high in the case of Mauna Kea, measured from the sea floor. On Venus, these volcanoes can cover hundreds of kilometres in area, but they are relatively flat, with an average height of 1.5 km (0.93 mi). Large volcanoes cause the Venusian lithosphere to flex downward because of their enormous vertical loads, producing flexural moats and/or ring fractures around the edifices. Large volcano edifice loading also causes magma chambers to fracture in a sill-like pattern, affecting magma propagation beneath the surface.Other unique features of Venus's surface are novae (radial networks of dikes or grabens) and arachnoids. A nova is formed when large quantities of magma are extruded onto the surface to form radiating ridges and trenches which are highly reflective to radar. These dikes form a symmetrical network around the central point where the lava emerged, where there may also be a depression caused by the collapse of the magma chamber.
Arachnoids are so named because they resemble a spider's web, featuring several concentric ovals surrounded by a complex network of radial fractures similar to those of a nova. It is not known whether the 250 or so features identified as arachnoids actually share a common origin, or are the result of different geological processes.

Recent volcanic activity
Volcanism on Venus has taken place within the last 2.5 million years; however, until recently there had been no absolute proof that any volcano on Venus has erupted recently. Recent radar imagery shows more than 1,000 volcanic structures and evidence of possible periodic resurfacing of the planet by floods of lava. In addition to the radar images, there is supporting evidence that volcanism has taken place, including an unusual change in the amount of sulphur dioxide gas in the upper atmosphere. Sulphur dioxide is an important component of volcanic outgassing.  However, the sulphur dioxide in the lower atmosphere remains stable. This could mean that a change in the global atmosphere caused the sulphur dioxide concentration to increase above the clouds.  Even though the change in the atmosphere may be evidence that there have been volcanoes that erupted in Venus, it is difficult to determine whether they occurred or not.  In March 2014, the first direct evidence for ongoing volcanism was located, in the form of infrared "flashes" over the edges of rift zone Ganis Chasma, near the shield volcano Sapas Mons. These flashes were detectable during two or three consecutive Earth days in 2008 and 2009 and are thought to be caused either by hot gases or lava released from volcanic eruptions. Scientists suspect that there are four volcanoes that may be active: Maat Mons, Ozza Mons, Sapas Mons and Idunn Mons.In 2020, a study by University of Maryland supported by Swiss National Science Foundation and NASA discovered that 37 of Venus's coronae show signs of ongoing activity. Maryland professor Laurent Montesi said, "we are able to point to specific structures and say 'Look, this is not an ancient volcano but one that is active today, dormant perhaps, but not dead...'" The active coronae are clustered near each other, so positioning geologic survey instruments would now be easier.In March 2023, at the 54th Lunar Planetary Science Conference, a team revealed the first images of volcanic activity on the surface of Venus. The announcement consisted of two radar images from different cycles of Magellan data (8 months apart) that displayed a volcanic vent that had expanded by almost 2 square kilometers. This data was over 30 years old at the time of this discovery. The scientists checked that this expansion could not be explained by the angle at which the images were taken through computer simulations which revealed that the change must be structural.

Lightning
Lightning on Venus may serve as a diagnostic of volcanism or atmospheric convection, so some effort has been devoted to detecting possible lightning on Venus. No lightning has been directly observed, but the most compelling evidence is the very low frequency (VLF) radio emissions recorded beneath the c",". However, the thick atmosphere of Venus makes it difficult to observe lightning directly. In fact, no direct evidence of lightning on Venus has been found so far.

One reason for the lack of direct observations is that the clouds on Venus are composed of sulfuric acid, which can absorb and scatter light. This makes it challenging to detect the faint flashes of lightning against the bright background of the clouds.

However, indirect evidence suggests that lightning may occur on Venus. For example, the presence of sulfur dioxide in the atmosphere, which is a byproduct of volcanic activity, suggests that there may be active volcanoes on the planet. Volcanic eruptions can generate electrical charges that could lead to lightning.

Additionally, the presence of convective clouds on Venus indicates the possibility of atmospheric convection, which is a process that can generate thunderstorms and lightning on Earth. These convective clouds are characterized by their cauliflower-like appearance and can reach altitudes of up to 70 kilometers (43 miles) above the surface.

To detect lightning on Venus, scientists have used instruments such as radio antennas to search for the characteristic radio signals produced by lightning discharges. However, these efforts have not yet yielded conclusive evidence of lightning on the planet.

Future missions to Venus, such as NASA's upcoming VERITAS and DAVINCI+ missions, may provide more insights into the presence of lightning on Venus. These missions will study the planet's atmosphere and surface in detail, which could help unravel the mysteries of Venusian lightning."],"response":null}

"Jumlah kawah tumbukan yang sedikit di permukaan Venus sebenarnya indikasi adanya pembaharuan permukaan yang relatif baru. **Jenis-Jenis Gunung Berapi di Venus: Kembaran yang Berbeda**

"Sekarang, mari kita bicara tentang jenis-jenis gunung berapi di Venus," kata Dr. Arya. "Di Bumi, kita punya gunung berapi perisai seperti di Hawaii, dan stratovolcano atau komposit seperti Gunung St. Helens. Nah, di Venus, sebagian besar adalah gunung berapi perisai juga."

Veronica mengangkat tangan. "Tapi bedanya apa, Dok?"

"Pertanyaan bagus, Veronica!" Dr. Arya mengangguk. "Di Bumi, gunung berapi perisai seperti Mauna Kea bisa sangat tinggi, puluhan kilometer lebar dan hingga 10 km tingginya jika diukur dari dasar laut. Lava mereka relatif encer, memungkinkan gas mudah keluar. Stratovolcano, di sisi lain, terkait dengan lempeng tektonik. Ketika kerak samudera menyelip ke bawah kerak lain, bersama dengan air laut, menghasilkan lava yang lebih kental, yang seringkali meletus dengan lebih dahsyat karena gas terperangkap."

"Nah, di Venus," Dr. Arya melanjutkan, "tidak ada lempeng tektonik atau air laut. Jadi, sebagian besar gunung berapi adalah tipe perisai. Namun, bentuknya berbeda! Karena gravitasi Venus dan tekanan atmosfer yang sangat tinggi membuat lava menyebar lebih luas dan membentuk struktur yang lebih rendah."

"Tapi, ada juga jenis gunung berapi yang unik di Venus, yang tidak kita temukan di Bumi," Dr. Arya melanjutkan dengan semangat. "Pertama, ada yang disebut **kubah pancake**."

Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar kubah-kubah besar yang terlihat seperti tumpukan pancake raksasa. "Kubah-kubah ini bisa berdiameter hingga 15 km dan tingginya kurang dari 1 km. Veronica terkesima. **Kubah pancake**! Nama itu sendiri sudah menarik.

"Kedua, ada struktur yang kami sebut 'kutu' atau **scalloped margin domes**," lanjut Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar kubah dengan 'kaki-kaki' yang tidak beraturan. "Selain itu, ada juga fitur seperti **novae**," Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar pola retakan radial. "Ini adalah jaringan saluran magma atau graben yang memancar keluar. Terbentuk ketika sejumlah besar magma keluar ke permukaan, membentuk punggung dan parit radial yang sangat memantulkan radar."

"Terakhir, ada **arachnoids**," Dr. Arya menunjukkan gambar pola seperti jaring laba-laba. "Dinamai demikian karena bentuknya menyerupai jaring laba-laba, dengan beberapa oval konsentris yang dikelilingi oleh jaringan retakan radial yang kompleks, mirip **nova**. Belum pasti apakah semua arachnoids memiliki asal yang sama atau hasil dari proses geologi yang berbeda."

**Misteri Sambaran Petir dan Peran Atmosfer**

"Veronica, tahukah kamu mengapa kita belum bisa langsung melihat kilat di Venus?" Dr. Arya bertanya.

Veronica mengerutkan kening. "Karena awan tebalnya, Dok?"

"Tepat sekali!" Dr. Arya mengacungkan jempol. "Atmosfer Venus yang kaya karbon dioksida sangat padat, 90 kali lipat dari Bumi. Awan-awannya terbuat dari asam sulfat, yang menyerap dan menyebarkan cahaya, membuat kilatan petir sulit terlihat."

"Tapi, ada bukti tidak langsung bahwa petir mungkin terjadi di sana," Dr. Arya melanjutkan. "Misalnya, perubahan jumlah gas sulfur dioksida di atmosfer atas dapat menunjukkan aktivitas vulkanik. Letusan vulkanik dapat menghasilkan muatan listrik yang memicu petir."

"Juga, awan konvektif di Venus, yang terlihat seperti kembang kol dan bisa mencapai ketinggian 70 km, menunjukkan kemungkinan adanya konveksi atmosfer, proses yang di Bumi menghasilkan badai petir," jelas Dr. Arya. "Namun, upaya mendeteksi petir secara langsung dengan gelombang radio frekuensi sangat rendah (VLF) belum membuahkan hasil pasti."

Venus has an atmosphere rich in carbon dioxide, with a density that is 90 times that of Earth's atmosphere.
There are over 80,000 volcanoes on Venus detected through radar mapping. For many years scientists debated on whether Venus was currently active or if the volcanic structures were remnants from the past. There are few impact craters on Venus' surface which pointed to relatively recent resurfacing. The most likely resurfacing event would have been volcanic flows.  Radar sounding by the Magellan probe revealed evidence for comparatively recent volcanic activity at Venus's highest volcano Maat Mons, in the form of ash flows near the summit and on the northern flank. Although many lines of evidence such as this suggest that volcanoes on Venus have been recently active, present-day eruptions at Maat Mons have not been confirmed. Nevertheless, other more recent studies, in January 2020, suggest that Venus, though not Maat Mons specifically, is indeed currently volcanically active. In 2023, scientists reexamined topographical images of the Maat Mons region taken by the Magellan orbiter. Using computer simulations they determined that the topography had changed during an 8-month interval, and have concluded that active volcanism was the cause. Until 2023 there had only been hints of active volcanism; announced in March 2023 scientists imaged a vent expanding in Magellan images which is the proof needed to announce active volcanism

Types of volcanoes
Venus has shield volcanoes, widespread lava flows and some unusual volcanoes called pancake domes and "tick-like" structures which are not present on Earth. Pancake dome volcanoes are up to 15 km (9.3 mi) in diameter and less than 1 km (0.62 mi) in height and are 100 times larger than lava domes formed on Earth. They are usually associated with coronae and tesserae (large regions of highly deformed terrain, folded and fractured in two or three dimensions, which are unique to Venus). The pancakes are thought to be formed by highly viscous, silica-rich lava erupting under Venus's high atmospheric pressure.

The "tick-like" structures are called scalloped margin domes. They are commonly called ticks because they appear as domes with numerous legs. They are thought to have undergone mass wasting events such as landslides on their margins. Sometimes deposits of debris can be seen scattered around them.

On Earth, volcanoes are mainly of two types: shield volcanoes and composite or stratovolcanoes.  The shield volcanoes, for example those in Hawaii, eject magma from the depths of the Earth in zones called hot spots.  The lava from these volcanoes is relatively fluid and permits the escape of gases.  Composite volcanoes, such as Mount St. Helens and Mount Pinatubo, are associated with tectonic plates.  In this type of volcano, the oceanic crust of one plate is sliding underneath the other in a subduction zone, together with an inflow of seawater, producing a gummier lava that restricts the exit of the gases, and for that reason, composite volcanoes tend to erupt more violently.

On Venus, where there are no tectonic plates or seawater, volcanoes are mostly of the shield type. Nevertheless, the morphology of volcanoes on Venus is different: on Earth, shield volcanoes can be a few tens of kilometres wide and up to 10 km (6.2 mi) high in the case of Mauna Kea, measured from the sea floor. On Venus, these volcanoes can cover hundreds of kilometres in area, but they are relatively flat, with an average height of 1.5 km (0.93 mi). Large volcanoes cause the Venusian lithosphere to flex downward because of their enormous vertical loads, producing flexural moats and/or ring fractures around the edifices. Large volcano edifice loading also causes magma chambers to fracture in a sill-like pattern, affecting magma propagation beneath the surface.Other unique features of Venus's surface are novae (radial networks of dikes or grabens) and arachnoids. A nova is formed when large quantities of magma are extruded onto the surface to form radiating ridges and trenches which are highly reflective to radar. These dikes form a symmetrical network around the central point where the lava emerged, where there may also be a depression caused by the collapse of the magma chamber.
Arachnoids are so named because they resemble a spider's web, featuring several concentric ovals surrounded by a complex network of radial fractures similar to those of a nova. It is not known whether the 250 or so features identified as arachnoids actually share a common origin, or are the result of different geological processes.

Volcanism on Venus has taken place within the last 2.5 million years; however, until recently there had been no absolute proof that any volcano on Venus has erupted recently. Recent radar imagery shows more than 1,000 volcanic structures and evidence of possible periodic resurfacing of the planet by floods of lava. In addition to the radar images, there is supporting evidence that volcanism has taken place, including an unusual change in the amount of sulphur dioxide gas in the upper atmosphere. Sulphur dioxide is an important component of volcanic outgassing.  However, the sulphur dioxide in the lower atmosphere remains stable. This could mean that a change in the global atmosphere caused the sulphur dioxide concentration to increase above the clouds.  Even though the change in the atmosphere may be evidence that there have been volcanoes that erupted in Venus, it is difficult to determine whether they occurred or not.  In March 2014, the first direct evidence for ongoing volcanism was located, in the form of infrared "flashes" over the edges of rift zone Ganis Chasma, near the shield volcano Sapas Mons. These flashes were detectable during two or three consecutive Earth days in 2008 and 2009 and are thought to be caused either by hot gases or lava released from volcanic eruptions. Scientists suspect that there are four volcanoes that may be active: Maat Mons, Ozza Mons, Sapas Mons and Idunn Mons.In 2020, a study by University of Maryland supported by Swiss National Science Foundation and NASA discovered that 37 of Venus's coronae show signs of ongoing activity. Maryland professor Laurent Montesi said, "we are able to point to specific structures and say 'Look, this is not an ancient volcano but one that is active today, dormant perhaps, but not dead...'" The active coronae are clustered near each other, so positioning geologic survey instruments would now be easier.In March 2023, at the 54th Lunar Planetary Science Conference, a team revealed the first images of volcanic activity on the surface of Venus. The announcement consisted of two radar images from different cycles of Magellan data (8 months apart) that displayed a volcanic vent that had expanded by almost 2 square kilometers. This data was over 30 years old at the time of this discovery. The scientists checked that this expansion could not be explained by the angle at which the images were taken through computer simulations which revealed that the change must be structural.

Lightning
Lightning on Venus may serve as a diagnostic of volcanism or atmospheric convection, so some effort has been devoted to detecting possible lightning on Venus. No lightning has been directly observed, but the most compelling evidence is the very low frequency (VLF) radio emissions recorded beneath the c",". However, the thick atmosphere of Venus makes it difficult to observe lightning directly. In fact, no direct evidence of lightning on Venus has been found so far.

One reason for the lack of direct observations is that the clouds on Venus are composed of sulfuric acid, which can absorb and scatter light. This makes it challenging to detect the faint flashes of lightning against the bright background of the clouds.

However, indirect evidence suggests that lightning may occur on Venus. For example, the presence of sulfur dioxide in the atmosphere, which is a byproduct of volcanic activity, suggests that there may be active volcanoes on the planet. Volcanic eruptions can generate electrical charges that could lead to lightning.

Additionally, the presence of convective clouds on Venus indicates the possibility of atmospheric convection, which is a process that can generate thunderstorms and lightning on Earth. These convective clouds are characterized by their cauliflower-like appearance and can reach altitudes of up to 70 kilometers (43 miles) above the surface.

To detect lightning on Venus, scientists have used instruments such as radio antennas to search for the characteristic radio signals produced by lightning discharges. However, these efforts have not yet yielded conclusive evidence of lightning on the planet.

Future missions to Venus, such as NASA's upcoming VERITAS and DAVINCI+ missions, may provide more insights into the presence of lightning on Venus. {"item_idx":47,"source":"Volcanism on Venus","language":"id","question_raw":"Question: What types of volcanoes are found on Venus, and how do they differ from those on Earth?","question":"What types of volcanoes are found on Venus, and how do they differ from those on Earth?","user_message":"Buat cerita edukatif yang membantu siswa memahami: What types of volcanoes are found on Venus, and how do they differ from those on Earth?","context_type":"v1+v2_merged_dedup","merged_contexts":["The surface of Venus is dominated by volcanic features and has more volcanoes than any other planet in the Solar System. It has a surface that is 90% basalt, and about 65% of the planet consists of a mosaic of volcanic lava plains, indicating that volcanism played a major role in shaping its surface. There are more than 1,000 volcanic structures and possible periodic resurfacing of Venus by floods of lava. The planet may have had a major global resurfacing event about 500 million years ago, from what scientists can tell from the density of impact craters on the surface. Venus has an atmosphere rich in carbon dioxide, with a density that is 90 times that of Earth's atmosphere.
There are over 80,000 volcanoes on Venus detected through radar mapping. For many years scientists debated on whether Venus was currently active or if the volcanic structures were remnants from the past. There are few impact craters on Venus' surface which pointed to relatively recent resurfacing. The most likely resurfacing event would have been volcanic flows.  Radar sounding by the Magellan probe revealed evidence for comparatively recent volcanic activity at Venus's highest volcano Maat Mons, in the form of ash flows near the summit and on the northern flank. Although many lines of evidence such as this suggest that volcanoes on Venus have been recently active, present-day eruptions at Maat Mons have not been confirmed. Nevertheless, other more recent studies, in January 2020, suggest that Venus, though not Maat Mons specifically, is indeed currently volcanically active. In 2023, scientists reexamined topographical images of the Maat Mons region taken by the Magellan orbiter. Using computer simulations they determined that the topography had changed during an 8-month interval, and have concluded that active volcanism was the cause. Until 2023 there had only been hints of active volcanism; announced in March 2023 scientists imaged a vent expanding in Magellan images which is the proof needed to announce active volcanism

Types of volcanoes
Venus has shield volcanoes, widespread lava flows and some unusual volcanoes called pancake domes and "tick-like" structures which are not present on Earth. Pancake dome volcanoes are up to 15 km (9.3 mi) in diameter and less than 1 km (0.62 mi) in height and are 100 times larger than lava domes formed on Earth. They are usually associated with coronae and tesserae (large regions of highly deformed terrain, folded and fractured in two or three dimensions, which are unique to Venus). The pancakes are thought to be formed by highly viscous, silica-rich lava erupting under Venus's high atmospheric pressure.

The "tick-like" structures are called scalloped margin domes. They are commonly called ticks because they appear as domes with numerous legs. They are thought to have undergone mass wasting events such as landslides on their margins. Sometimes deposits of debris can be seen scattered around them.

On Earth, volcanoes are mainly of two types: shield volcanoes and composite or stratovolcanoes.  The shield volcanoes, for example those in Hawaii, eject magma from the depths of the Earth in zones called hot spots.  The lava from these volcanoes is relatively fluid and permits the escape of gases.  Composite volcanoes, such as Mount St. Helens and Mount Pinatubo, are associated with tectonic plates.  In this type of volcano, the oceanic crust of one plate is sliding underneath the other in a subduction zone, together with an inflow of seawater, producing a gummier lava that restricts the exit of the gases, and for that reason, composite volcanoes tend to erupt more violently.

On Venus, where there are no tectonic plates or seawater, volcanoes are mostly of the shield type. Nevertheless, the morphology of volcanoes on Venus is different: on Earth, shield volcanoes can be a few tens of kilometres wide and up to 10 km (6.2 mi) high in the case of Mauna Kea, measured from the sea floor. On Venus, these volcanoes can cover hundreds of kilometres in area, but they are relatively flat, with an average height of 1.5 km (0.93 mi). Large volcanoes cause the Venusian lithosphere to flex downward because of their enormous vertical loads, producing flexural moats and/or ring fractures around the edifices. Large volcano edifice loading also causes magma chambers to fracture in a sill-like pattern, affecting magma propagation beneath the surface.Other unique features of Venus's surface are novae (radial networks of dikes or grabens) and arachnoids. A nova is formed when large quantities of magma are extruded onto the surface to form radiating ridges and trenches which are highly reflective to radar. These dikes form a symmetrical network around the central point where the lava emerged, where there may also be a depression caused by the collapse of the magma chamber.
Arachnoids are so named because they resemble a spider's web, featuring several concentric ovals surrounded by a complex network of radial fractures similar to those of a nova. It is not known whether the 250 or so features identified as arachnoids actually share a common origin, or are the result of different geological processes.

Recent volcanic activity
Volcanism on Venus has taken place within the last 2.5 million years; however, until recently there had been no absolute proof that any volcano on Venus has erupted recently. Recent radar imagery shows more than 1,000 volcanic structures and evidence of possible periodic resurfacing of the planet by floods of lava. In addition to the radar images, there is supporting evidence that volcanism has taken place, including an unusual change in the amount of sulphur dioxide gas in the upper atmosphere. Sulphur dioxide is an important component of volcanic outgassing.  However, the sulphur dioxide in the lower atmosphere remains stable. This could mean that a change in the global atmosphere caused the sulphur dioxide concentration to increase above the clouds.  Even though the change in the atmosphere may be evidence that there have been volcanoes that erupted in Venus, it is difficult to determine whether they occurred or not.  In March 2014, the first direct evidence for ongoing volcanism was located, in the form of infrared "flashes" over the edges of rift zone Ganis Chasma, near the shield volcano Sapas Mons. These flashes were detectable during two or three consecutive Earth days in 2008 and 2009 and are thought to be caused either by hot gases or lava released from volcanic eruptions. Scientists suspect that there are four volcanoes that may be active: Maat Mons, Ozza Mons, Sapas Mons and Idunn Mons.In 2020, a study by University of Maryland supported by Swiss National Science Foundation and NASA discovered that 37 of Venus's coronae show signs of ongoing activity. Maryland professor Laurent Montesi said, "we are able to point to specific structures and say 'Look, this is not an ancient volcano but one that is active today, dormant perhaps, but not dead...'" The active coronae are clustered near each other, so positioning geologic survey instruments would now be easier.In March 2023, at the 54th Lunar Planetary Science Conference, a team revealed the first images of volcanic activity on the surface of Venus. The announcement consisted of two radar images from different cycles of Magellan data (8 months apart) that displayed a volcanic vent that had expanded by almost 2 square kilometers. This data was over 30 years old at the time of this discovery. The scientists checked that this expansion could not be explained by the angle at which the images were taken through computer simulations which revealed that the change must be structural.

Lightning
Lightning on Venus may serve as a diagnostic of volcanism or atmospheric convection, so some effort has been devoted to detecting possible lightning on Venus. No lightning has been directly observed, but the most compelling evidence is the very low frequency (VLF) radio emissions recorded beneath the c",". However, the thick atmosphere of Venus makes it difficult to observe lightning directly. In fact, no direct evidence of lightning on Venus has been found so far.

One reason for the lack of direct observations is that the clouds on Venus are composed of sulfuric acid, which can absorb and scatter light. This makes it challenging to detect the faint flashes of lightning against the bright background of the clouds.

However, indirect evidence suggests that lightning may occur on Venus. For example, the presence of sulfur dioxide in the atmosphere, which is a byproduct of volcanic activity, suggests that there may be active volcanoes on the planet. Volcanic eruptions can generate electrical charges that could lead to lightning.

Additionally, the presence of convective clouds on Venus indicates the possibility of atmospheric convection, which is a process that can generate thunderstorms and lightning on Earth. These convective clouds are characterized by their cauliflower-like appearance and can reach altitudes of up to 70 kilometers (43 miles) above the surface.

To detect lightning on Venus, scientists have used instruments such as radio antennas to search for the characteristic radio signals produced by lightning discharges. However, these efforts have not yet yielded conclusive evidence of lightning on the planet.

Future missions to Venus, such as NASA's upcoming VERITAS and DAVINCI+ missions, may provide more insights into the presence of lightning on Venus. These missions will study the planet's atmosphere and surface in detail, which could help unravel the mysteries of Venusian lightning."]}

{"final_story":"## Petualangan Vulkanik Veronica: Menguak Misteri Gunung Berapi Venus

Veronica, seorang siswi SMA pecinta sains, duduk di kursinya dengan mata berbinar. Di layar depan, presentasi geologi planetarium menunjukkan gambar planet Venus yang diselimuti awan tebal. Veronica sudah tahu Venus panas, tapi ia tidak menyangka presentasi Dr. Arya akan membawanya pada topik yang sangat ia gemari: vulkanisme. "Tahukah kalian," Dr. Arya melanjutkan, "permukaan Venus didominasi oleh fitur-fitur vulkanik. Bayangkan, ada lebih dari 80.000 gunung berapi di Venus! Jauh lebih banyak dari planet lain."

Veronica mencatat dengan antusias. "Dan yang lebih menarik," kata Dr. Arya, "sekitar 65% permukaan Venus terdiri dari dataran lava vulkanik, menunjukkan bahwa gunung berapi telah membentuk permukaannya secara masif."

"Jumlah kawah tumbukan yang sedikit di permukaan Venus sebenarnya indikasi adanya pembaharuan permukaan yang relatif baru. "Sekarang, mari kita bicara tentang jenis-jenis gunung berapi di Venus," kata Dr. Arya. "Di Bumi, kita punya gunung berapi perisai seperti di Hawaii, dan stratovolcano atau komposit seperti Gunung St. Helens. Nah, di Venus, sebagian besar adalah gunung berapi perisai juga."

"Di Bumi, gunung berapi perisai seperti Mauna Kea bisa sangat tinggi, puluhan kilometer lebar dan hingga 10 km tingginya jika diukur dari dasar laut. Ketika kerak samudera menyelip ke bawah kerak lain, bersama dengan air laut, menghasilkan lava yang lebih kental, yang seringkali meletus dengan lebih dahsyat karena gas terperangkap."

"Nah, di Venus," Dr. Arya melanjutkan, "tidak ada lempeng tektonik atau air laut. Jadi, sebagian besar gunung berapi adalah tipe perisai. Namun, bentuknya berbeda! Meskipun bisa menutupi area ratusan kilometer, gunung berapi perisai Venus relatif datar, dengan tinggi rata-rata hanya 1,5 km. Kenapa? Karena gravitasi Venus dan tekanan atmosfer yang sangat tinggi membuat lava menyebar lebih luas dan membentuk struktur yang lebih rendah."

"Tapi, ada juga jenis gunung berapi yang unik di Venus, yang tidak kita temukan di Bumi," Dr. Arya melanjutkan dengan semangat. "Pertama, ada yang disebut **kubah pancake**."

Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar kubah-kubah besar yang terlihat seperti tumpukan pancake raksasa. "Kubah-kubah ini bisa berdiameter hingga 15 km dan tingginya kurang dari 1 km. Mereka seratus kali lebih besar dari kubah lava di Bumi! Mereka terbentuk oleh lava yang sangat kental, kaya silika, yang meletus di bawah tekanan atmosfer Venus yang sangat tinggi."

Veronica terkesima. **Kubah pancake**! Nama itu sendiri sudah menarik.

"Kedua, ada struktur yang kami sebut 'kutu' atau **scalloped margin domes**," lanjut Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar kubah dengan 'kaki-kaki' yang tidak beraturan. "Mereka terlihat seperti kutu raksasa karena memiliki banyak 'kaki' di sekelilingnya. Diyakini, 'kaki' ini terbentuk akibat peristiwa longsoran di tepiannya, dan kita sering melihat puing-puing berserakan di sekitarnya."

"Selain itu, ada juga fitur seperti **novae**," Dr. Arya menampilkan gambar pola retakan radial. "Ini adalah jaringan saluran magma atau graben yang memancar keluar. Terbentuk ketika sejumlah besar magma keluar ke permukaan, membentuk punggung dan parit radial yang sangat memantulkan radar."

"Terakhir, ada **arachnoids**," Dr. Arya menunjukkan gambar pola seperti jaring laba-laba. "Dinamai demikian karena bentuknya menyerupai jaring laba-laba, dengan beberapa oval konsentris yang dikelilingi oleh jaringan retakan radial yang kompleks, mirip **nova**. Belum pasti apakah semua arachnoids memiliki asal yang sama atau hasil dari proses geologi yang berbeda."

**Misteri Sambaran Petir dan Peran Atmosfer**

"Veronica, tahukah kamu mengapa kita belum bisa langsung melihat kilat di Venus?" Dr. Arya bertanya.

Veronica mengerutkan kening. "Karena awan tebalnya, Dok?"

"Tepat sekali!" Dr. Arya mengacungkan jempol. "Atmosfer Venus yang kaya karbon dioksida sangat padat, 90 kali lipat dari Bumi. Awan-awannya terbuat dari asam sulfat, yang menyerap dan menyebarkan cahaya, membuat kilatan petir sulit terlihat."

"Tapi, ada bukti tidak langsung bahwa petir mungkin terjadi di sana," Dr. Arya melanjutkan. "Misalnya, perubahan jumlah gas sulfur dioksida di atmosfer atas dapat menunjukkan aktivitas vulkanik. Letusan vulkanik dapat menghasilkan muatan listrik yang memicu petir."

"Juga, awan konvektif di Venus, yang terlihat seperti kembang kol dan bisa mencapai ketinggian 70 km, menunjukkan kemungkinan adanya konveksi atmosfer, proses yang di Bumi menghasilkan badai petir," jelas Dr. Arya. "Namun, upaya mendeteksi petir secara langsung dengan gelombang radio frekuensi sangat rendah (VLF) belum membuahkan hasil pasti."

"Misi-misi masa depan ke Venus, seperti VERITAS dan DAVINCI+ dari NASA, diharapkan bisa mengungkap misteri ini," Dr. Arya mengakhiri presentasinya. "Mereka akan mempelajari atmosfer dan permukaan Venus secara detail, mungkin akan menjawab pertanyaan tentang petir di sana."

Veronica sekarang memiliki gambaran yang jauh lebih jelas tentang Venus. Ia tidak hanya belajar tentang jenis-jenis gunung berapi yang unik di sana—kubah pancake dan 'kutu'—tetapi juga perbedaan mereka dengan gunung berapi Bumi, dipengaruhi oleh ketiadaan lempeng tektonik, tekanan atmosfer yang tinggi, dan komposisi lava. Ada 22 patung seperti itu, juga mengenakan baju zirah, masing-masing dengan ekspresi kesedihan yang mendalam, seolah meratapi sosok yang bersemayam di bawahnya.

"Dari semua detail ini, apa yang bisa kamu simpulkan, Lia?" tanya Bapak Harris. "Siapa kira-kira orang penting yang dimakamkan di sini?"

Lia menunjuk tulisan Latin yang terukir di tepi lempengan batu di bawah efiji. "Ada inskripsi di sini, Pak. Meskipun saya tidak terlalu fasih bahasa Latin, saya melihat nama 'Alexander Senescallus, Dominus De Badenoch'. Dan di bawahnya, ada tanggal 'Anno Domini 1394'."

Bapak Harris tersenyum. "Tepat sekali! Inskripsi itu berbunyi: 'Di sini bersemayam Lord Alexander Stewart, Lord of Badenoch, yang dikenang baik, yang meninggal pada tanggal 24 Juli, tahun Tuhan 1394.' Jadi, yang dimakamkan di sini adalah Alexander Stewart, Earl of Buchan, yang meninggal sekitar tahun 1394."

"Ah, itu pertanyaan bagus, Lia!" seru Bapak Harris. "Alexander Stewart memang dikenal sebagai 'Wolf of Badenoch', atau Serigala dari Badenoch. Dia adalah putra ketiga Raja Robert II dari Skotlandia, yang selamat hingga dewasa. Julukan itu diberikan karena reputasinya yang sangat buruk, bahkan digambarkan sebagai 'musuh Gereja' dan 'pria paling keji di Skotlandia' pada tahun 2017."

"Sebab, ia dikenal karena kekejamannya yang ternama," jelas Bapak Harris, dengan nada serius. "Salah satu perbuatannya yang paling terkenal adalah penghancuran kota kerajaan Elgin dan katedralnya yang dibangun pada abad ke-13, pada bulan Mei 1370. "Benar," kata Bapak Harris. "Efiji ini rusak parah sekitar tahun 1560, selama Reformasi Skotlandia. Sekarang, efiji ini terbagi menjadi empat bagian terpisah: di bagian leher, pinggang, lutut, dan pergelangan kaki. Kaki kanannya hilang, dan wajah serta kaki kirinya rusak parah. Meskipun demikian, ironisnya, ini masih menjadi salah satu patung kerajaan Skotlandia abad pertengahan yang paling terawat."

Lia menyentuh salah satu bagian yang retak. Detail baju zirahnya, seperti helm bascinet, pelindung bahu pauldron, dan pelat dada, masih terlihat, meskipun tak lagi utuh.

"Lalu, pleurants di makam peti ini?" tanya Lia, menunjuk patung-patung kecil yang menghiasi sisi-sisi makam.

"Makam peti ini berlapis 22 pleurants yang juga mengenakan baju zirah, delapan di setiap sisi panjang dan tiga di setiap ujung," jelas Bapak Harris. "Mereka ditempatkan di bawah kanopi tiga-lengkung dan dipisahkan oleh penyangga kecil."

It is located in Dunkeld Cathedral, Perthshire, Scotland, and was built for Alexander Stewart, Earl of Buchan (1343 – c. 1394), who is buried underneath.The effigy is placed on top of the altar tomb, and shows Stuart in full and highly detailed knightly armour, with a lion (or dog) resting at his feet. It is in poor condition having been broken apart and defaced in the 16th century during the Scottish Reformation. The effigy is placed on top of an altar tomb lined with 22 pleurants (or "weepers"), who are also dressed in armour.

Alexander Stewart, the Wolf of Badenoch
Stuart was the third surviving son  son of king Robert II of Scotland (1316 – 1390). He is known to history as the deeply unpopular "Wolf of Badenoch", a name given due to  his notorious cruelty, in particular for his destruction of the royal burgh of Elgin and its 13th-century cathedral in May 1370, for which he earned a reputation as "an enemy of the Church", and was described in 2017 as "Scothland's vilest man".

Description
The tomb is inscribed with the year 1420.The monument remains in its origional position behind the choir screen at the east-end of the cathedral, while Stuart's grave is underneath.

Effigy
The effigy is made from grey–green marble and measures 7 ft (2.1 m) in length. Stewart lies on a cloak and is dressed in full armour with his sword by his left slide. His head is protected by a bascinet (an open-faced combat helmet) and visor and he wears a pauldron—a type of spaulder covering the shoulders. He has a breastplate over his torso, above a plate-skirt at his hips. He has a hip-belt of a type worn in Scotland until the end of the 15th century.The animal resting at his feet may be a lion, or—less likely—a dog.
The effigy is in poor condition, having been damaged c. 1560 during the Scottish Reformation. It now consists of four separate pieces having been broken apart at the neck, waist, knees and ankles. His right foot is missing and his face and left foot are severely damaged. However, it remains one of the best preserved pieces of royal medieval Scottish sculpture.

Altar tomb
The altar (or "chest") tomb contains 22 pleurants (or "weepers", that is sculpted figures representing mourners) dressed in armour; eight on each long-side and three at each end. These figures are positioned under three-arch canopies and separated by small buttresses.The Latin inscription is placed on the edge of the stone slab below the effigy. It reads, "His Jacet Domninus Alexander Senescallus, Dominus De Badenoch, Bonæ Memorle, Qui Obit 24 Die Mensis Julii, Anno Domini 1394".

It is located in Dunkeld Cathedral, Perthshire, Scotland, and was built for Alexander Stewart, Earl of Buchan (1343 – c. 1394), who is buried underneath.The effigy is placed on top of the altar tomb, and shows Stuart in full and highly detailed knightly armour, with a lion (or dog) resting at his feet. Alexander Stewart, the Wolf of Badenoch
Stuart was the third surviving son  son of king Robert II of Scotland (1316 – 1390). He is known to history as the deeply unpopular "Wolf of Badenoch", a name given due to  his notorious cruelty, in particular for his destruction of the royal burgh of Elgin and its 13th-century cathedral in May 1370, for which he earned a reputation as "an enemy of the Church", and was described in 2017 as "Scothland's vilest man".

Description
The tomb is inscribed with the year 1420.The monument remains in its origional position behind the choir screen at the east-end of the cathedral, while Stuart's grave is underneath.

Effigy
The effigy is made from grey–green marble and measures 7 ft (2.1 m) in length. Stewart lies on a cloak and is dressed in full armour with his sword by his left slide. His head is protected by a bascinet (an open-faced combat helmet) and visor and he wears a pauldron—a type of spaulder covering the shoulders. He has a breastplate over his torso, above a plate-skirt at his hips. He has a hip-belt of a type worn in Scotland until the end of the 15th century.The animal resting at his feet may be a lion, or—less likely—a dog.
The effigy is in poor condition, having been damaged c. 1560 during the Scottish Reformation. It now consists of four separate pieces having been broken apart at the neck, waist, knees and ankles. His right foot is missing and his face and left foot are severely damaged. However, it remains one of the best preserved pieces of royal medieval Scottish sculpture.

Altar tomb
The altar (or "chest") tomb contains 22 pleurants (or "weepers", that is sculpted figures representing mourners) dressed in armour; eight on each long-side and three at each end. These figures are positioned under three-arch canopies and separated by small buttresses.The Latin inscription is placed on the edge of the stone slab below the effigy. It reads, "His Jacet Domninus Alexander Senescallus, Dominus De Badenoch, Bonæ Memorle, Qui Obit 24 Die Mensis Julii, Anno Domini 1394".

Lia mendekat, mengamati efiji itu lebih saksama. "Saya melihat banyak retakan, Pak. Sepertinya sudah terpecah-pecah."

Lia menyentuh salah satu bagian yang retak. Detail baju zirahnya, seperti helm bascinet, pelindung bahu pauldron, dan pelat dada, masih terlihat, meskipun tak lagi utuh.

"Makam peti ini berlapis 22 pleurants yang juga mengenakan baju zirah, delapan di setiap sisi panjang dan tiga di setiap ujung," jelas Bapak Harris. "Mereka ditempatkan di bawah kanopi tiga-lengkung dan dipisahkan oleh penyangga kecil."
